- Row 3 (Read range parameters). Files: src/tools/filesystem/read_file.zig, src/builtins/tools.zig. Change: read_file accepts line_offset (non-zero int; positive is the 1-based first line, negative reads the last N lines), column_offset (int >= 0, applied to the first line of a forward read), n_lines (int > 0, same as line_count), and max_chars (int > 0, capped at the existing 256 KiB output limit). start_line and line_count keep working; passing both start_line and line_offset is rejected. - Row 7 follow-up (Grep regex, multiline, count_matches). Files: src/core/shared/regex.zig (new), src/core/workspace/grep_search.zig, src/tools/filesystem/grep_files.zig, src/builtins/tools.zig, src/main.zig (test import). Change: pattern is a regex (ripgrep-style subset: literals, ., [classes], \d \w \s \b \B, groups and (?:), |, * + ? {m,n} with lazy suffix, ^ and $ as haystack anchors); an invalid pattern fails decode with "grep_files field \"pattern\" is not a valid regular expression". multiline true searches the whole file (16 MiB cap) with . matching newlines, and reports every line a match touches. count_matches prints "[grep] Found N total occurrences across M files for P" then path:count lines, paged by head_limit and offset; type is accepted with count_matches. Breaks: literal patterns containing metacharacters (. ( ) [ ] * + ? { | ^ $ \) now match as regex (a.b matches axb); count_matches counts occurrences, not matching lines; the count output wording changed; multiline is no longer rejected. Limits: byte-level matching (a non-ASCII class or . matches one byte); no lookaround or backreferences; in non-multiline mode a line longer than the 64 KiB read chunk is matched per chunk, so a match crossing the chunk boundary is missed. Witness (red before, green after): 'regex literals match leftmost occurrence', 'regex dot and quantifiers follow leftmost-first semantics', 'regex alternation and groups', 'regex classes escapes and anchors', 'regex case-insensitive folds ASCII letters', 'regex dot matches newline only when enabled', 'regex rejects malformed patterns', 'grep_files rejects Kimi parameter shapes it cannot honour or misreads', 'grep_files count_matches reports per-file occurrences restricted by type', 'grep_files multiline lets the pattern span lines and dot cross newlines', 'grep_files pattern is a regular expression', 'grep_files count mode reports exact matching lines beyond collection cap', 'grep search counts multiline occurrences and lists the file', 'grep search counts regex occurrences per line'.

## Second pass: Hooks
- Hooks shared (no user-visible change in this commit). Files: src/core/hooks/external.zig, src/core/hooks/definitions.zig, src/core/hooks/runtime.zig, src/core/hooks/hooks.zig, src/builtins/hooks/command.zig. ## Second pass: Plugins
- Plugins row 3 (partial). Files: src/core/plugins/manifest.zig. Change: the manifest now reads the hooks array (parsed by external.parseDefinitionsIn with cwd set to the plugin root), the commands field (a string or string[] of ./ paths; a directory is walked recursively for .md files, a .md file is taken directly; names are the path without .md, sorted by name; containment checked), and an object interface kept raw. Breaks: Manifest gains hooks, commands and interface fields with defaults; no caller reads them yet. Deviations: a hooks array with any invalid entry loads no plugin hooks (Kimi keeps the valid entries; rebuilding a json array per entry needs the std.json array constructor, which cannot be checked without a toolchain); interface.locales is not resolved (held with the locale reader, class b). Witness (red before, green after): "manifest reads hooks with the plugin root as their working directory", "manifest reports a non-array hooks field and loads no hooks", "manifest collects markdown commands from directories and files, sorted by name", "manifest rejects command paths that escape the plugin", "manifest keeps an object interface and ignores other shapes".
- Plugins row 9 (partial). Files: src/core/plugins/source.zig (new), src/core/plugins/manager.zig. Change: source.resolve classifies an absolute local path, an https URL, and a github.com repo URL (bare, tree/ref, releases/tag/tag, commit/sha; .git suffix stripped; percent-decoded ref segments; sha-like tree refs are sha kind; any other github path falls through to a zip URL). A relative path fails RelativePluginSource. install of a zip URL or a github source fails UnsupportedPluginSource. Held (class b): the zip download and the GitHub archive fetch, which need an HTTPS client call in core and the zip reader of row 10; the Phase A toolchain cannot check those APIs. Breaks: requireLocalSource is removed (its only caller was install); install takes an InstallOptions fifth argument (row 16). Witness (red before, green after): "source resolves github repo, tree, tag, commit and sha forms", "source decodes percent-encoded ref segments", "source keeps other https urls as zip URLs and rejects relative local paths", "install refuses relative sources and remote sources it cannot fetch" (extended with a github repo URL).
- Plugins row 10 (held, class b). Blocker: zip extraction needs std.zip with a path traversal guard and the single child directory root rule (Kimi archive.ts:34-146). The Phase A toolchain is not available to check the Zig 0.17 std.zip API, so no reader is written blind. The traversal guard is part of the same held unit.
- Plugins row 11 (coded). Files: src/core/plugins/manager.zig. Change: install takes InstallOptions.expected_id; a manifest id that differs from it (after normalisation) fails PluginIdMismatch before anything is copied. Breaks: the install signature gains a required fifth argument. Witness (red before, green after): "install checks the expected id before anything is copied".
- Plugins row 14 (held, class c). Owner: the slash surface (src/core/slash_commands/command_specs.zig, src/builtins/commands.zig, src/core/cli/cli_surface.zig, per AGENTS.md Adding a Command). ## Second pass: Built-in tools
- Built-in tools row 10 (partial). Files: src/tools/filesystem/read_media_file.zig (new), src/tools/filesystem/read_file.zig (readIntoBuffer and max_attach_image_bytes made pub for reuse), src/builtins/tools.zig (read_media_file spec, imports, all, advertisement_order, read_only_tool_names). Change: ReadMediaFile added with path, region (x and y at least 0, width and height at least 1, validated at decode) and full_resolution (boolean, validated). The non-crop path attaches an image (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, by magic bytes) unchanged as a rich tool image when it is within the 5 MiB encoded limit; over-limit images fail with the full_resolution or save-a-smaller-copy message; non-image files and directories fail. A call with region fails with the decoder reason. Breaks: ReadMediaFile joins the advertised set and the read-only set; the byte-exact model-facing contract hash in tools.zig test "built-in model-facing tool contract stays byte exact" must be regenerated in Phase B (not run in Phase A). vision is left as is: it is the runtime sub-model tool, withheld from default advertisement, and its contract lives in src/core/agent/runtime/vision_contracts.zig (runtime owner). Witness (red before, green after): read_media_file.zig tests "ReadMediaFile decodes path, region and full_resolution", "ReadMediaFile names the argument that fails validation", "ReadMediaFile holds region cropping until an image decoder exists", "ReadMediaFile attaches a PNG within the attach limit unchanged", "ReadMediaFile rejects a text file as not an image", "ReadMediaFile rejects an image over the attach limit and names full_resolution", "ReadMediaFile rejects a directory path"; tools.zig "ReadMediaFile is advertised beside read_file with path, region and full_resolution" and the updated "built-in read-only tool set matches plan inspection tools". Defects for the registry worker (owner: registry worker, the files are tool_dispatch.zig, tools.zig, model_tool_schema.zig):
- D1 tool_dispatch.zig ExecutorKind lacks create_goal, get_goal, set_goal_budget, update_goal. The four specs reference them, so the build breaks until they are added.
- D2 tool_dispatch.zig DispatchContext lacks a goal field. Add goal: ?goal_state.View = null, importing ../goal/state.zig. The session fills it per dispatch from its State, its allocator and its clock in ms. Leave it null for subagents: the executors then return "Goal tools are only supported by the main agent." This is Kimi's mainAgentOnly rule (Kimi agent/tools/mainAgentOnly.ts).
- D3 builtins/tools.zig does not list the four specs. Add goal_tools.create_goal, get_goal, set_goal_budget and update_goal, or goal_tools.all.
- D4 Stop flags have no consumer. After each call, honour goal_tools.stopsBatch(kind, input) (Kimi stopBatchAfterThis: skip the rest of the batch) and goal_tools.stopsTurn(kind, input) (Kimi stopTurn: end the turn). ToolResult has no stop field today. Owner: registry and agent loop.
- D5 Session persistence. Kimi writes goal.create, goal.update and goal.clear as durable events. fx has no goal events in the session log, so a resumed session loses its goal. Owner: session log (not in any wave-3 owner list), class (c).
- D6 model_tool_schema.JsonType has no number. SetGoalBudget.value is declared integer in the schema, while decode accepts any positive finite number as Kimi does. Model-facing schema is integer-only until a number type is added. Owner: registry worker, core/tooling/model_tool_schema.zig, class (c).

Not built here (class b or c, named):
- N1 Autonomous continuation driver (class b, feature fx lacks). Kimi goalService.ts launchContinuationTurn, handleTurnEnded, step-cap continuation, provider-error pauses (lines 530-830) and the wall-clock deadline timer (lines 984-1021). It runs in the agent loop, so the call sites are the hooks worker's agent loop files, class (c).
- N2 Accounting hooks. The caller must call State.recordTurn per goal turn, State.recordTokens per output usage, and State.enforceWallClockBudget on a timer. Kimi goalService.ts lines 500-530 and 598-633. Owner: agent loop, class (c).
- N3 Reminder injection. reminder.render and reminder.needsFullReminder are pure. The context builder must register them (Kimi goalInjection.ts GoalInjection), pass wait_for from ToolCapabilities.wait_for_enabled, and track the last disclosure and compaction. Owner: context builder, class (c).
- N4 Start permission prompt for CreateGoal (Kimi create-goal.ts goal_start display). Owner: permissions worker, Permission modes row 28, class (b).
- N5 /goal edit and the objective-edited check (Kimi isObjectiveEditedSinceTurnStart, goalService.ts 279-283). Depends on the slash command row 24, which is held, class (b).

Decided by parity (Kimi file:line):
- Completion clears the goal, so GetGoal returns null after complete (Kimi goalService.ts 457-471: markComplete calls clearInternal, which dispatches GoalClear). Blocked keeps the goal (goalService.ts 444-455).
- Goal tools need no approval (Kimi agent/permissionPolicy/policies/default-tool-approve.ts lists the goal tools). requires_approval is false.
- Turn-target rule. Kimi binds a goal tool to the goal that drives the current turn (goalTurnTargets, goalService.ts 274-277). fx has no goal-driven turns yet, so the goal id captured at decode must equal the current goal id at call. Stale calls return "the current goal changed", as in Kimi create-goal.ts, set-goal-budget.ts and update-goal.ts.
- Budget block reason text and the block prefix come from goalService.ts 1060-1072.

Known differences (defects, minor):
- Kimi JS trim() also strips Unicode whitespace. fx trims ASCII whitespace only.
- Kimi counts objective length in UTF-16 units and slices the completion criterion at unit 4000. fx counts UTF-16 units but truncates at a code point boundary, so an astral character at the cut keeps one unit less.
- Budgets are u64. Kimi accepts any finite positive number. fx reports a value at or above 2^64 as not a reasonable goal budget.
- Number text in messages uses Zig {d} for fractions. It matches JS String for ordinary values.
- Decode errors use one fixed message per tool. Kimi's zod text is not reproduced; Kimi does not fix that text, so the fixed message is the default.
- Action labels (Creating goal and so on) are fx short labels. Kimi's descriptions are Creating a goal and so on.

Tests were not run. Phase A forbids zig build and zig test. Each witness is a Zig test in the file named by the row.

Persist each line from runtime.drainJournal() to the session log in order. On restore, call runtime.replay(line) for each record before the first tick. A fork starts with an empty runtime and must not replay the source journal.

## Wave 3 addendum: Permission modes (Kimi's three semantics by parity)
- Permission modes row 1 (coded). Files: src/core/shared/types.zig (PermissionMode.parse, label), src/core/permissions/permissions.zig (permissionModeDisplayLabel), src/core/tooling/tool_admission.zig, src/core/permissions/permission_gate.zig, src/core/permissions/command_admission.zig. Change: fx has three modes with Kimi semantics: ask = manual (Always Ask), yolo = Ask When Needed, auto = Never Ask. Full access is retired, so the existing yolo tag is redefined as Kimi's yolo; no fourth tag is added (a fourth tag would keep a full-access meaning, which Kimi does not have, and would break exhaustive switches in the files outside the owned paths that the first-pass note counts at about 37). Decided by parity: three modes only, no full-access (Kimi permissionPolicy/types.ts:6 is `'manual' | 'yolo' | 'auto'`); labels Always Ask / Ask When Needed / Never Ask (apps/kimi-code/src/tui/utils/permission-mode.ts:4-6); default manual (agent/permissionMode/permissionModeOps.ts:23). Breaks: PermissionMode.parse("full-access") and parse("full access") now return null (they were yolo); parse("ask") still returns ask as an alias of manual. label(): ask is now "manual" (was "ask"), yolo is now "yolo" (was "full-access"). permissionModeDisplayLabel: ask "Always Ask", yolo "Ask When Needed", auto "Never Ask" (were "ask", "full access", "auto"). Behaviour: every caller of the yolo tag now gets Kimi yolo, not full access (see Breaks under rows 23 and 24). ## Wave 3: Subagents join tests (Unattributed files attributed, DEFECT closed for the three named tests)
- Subagents join tests (coded, tests only). Files: src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig (the three tests named in the DEFECT line, and the MailboxFixture test helper; no non-test code changed). Change: decided by parity: Kimi rejects an Agent call to a running agent with AGENT_ALREADY_RUNNING (packages/agent-core-v2/src/agent/tools/agent/agentTool.ts:413-416), so a message to a running child returns child_already_running and joins no turn. Test "a parent's message that joined a turn that failed runs as the child's next work" is replaced, because its whole purpose was the join, by "a parent's message to a running subagent is refused, and a failed turn does not carry it forward": the refusal is asserted, the failed turn is the only report, and a later message to the idle child starts a new work whose reply does not carry the refused text. Test "the parent's stop drops a message that joined the turn it stops" is replaced, because its whole purpose was the join, by "a parent's message to a running subagent is refused, and the parent's stop ends the turn without a report": the refusal is asserted, the stop path is kept (one run, zero reports, reply "Stopped reviewer: its turn ended."), and the drop assertion is removed because nothing joins to be dropped. Test "the parent's stop ends a turn the user started on the child's screen, which owes no report" keeps its name and stop path, with a reject step added while the user's turn runs: child_already_running is returned and the worker's queued prompt count stays 0. MailboxFixture: the steerable field and its beginDirectProcessing and finishProcessing use in run() are removed, since they existed only to let a message join a running turn. Breaks: none in non-test code. Witness (red before, green after; verified by reading only, not run in Phase A): 'a parent's message to a running subagent is refused, and a failed turn does not carry it forward', 'a parent's message to a running subagent is refused, and the parent's stop ends the turn without a report', and 'the parent's stop ends a turn the user started on the child's screen, which owes no report' (name kept, body changed). Count: 3 witnesses.

Tests: 'a message to a busy subagent waits and runs as its next work, in order' (expects "is busy" and two runs); 'a message past a busy subagent's full queue is refused to its sender' (expects queue_full); 'a user's stop drops the parent's messages waiting for a subagent, and its report says how many' (expects dropped=2); 'a user's stop of a work that owes no report tells the parent of its dropped messages' (expects the dropped text, dropped=1); 'a parent's message while the user's turn runs waits for it, then starts' (expects "is busy" and a second run); 'messages waiting for a busy subagent are taken into its next turn as one work' (expects "DONE second" followed by "third" in one turn); 'stop ends a subagent's turn without a report and drops what waits for it' (expects the dropped text); 'the parent's close ends a working subagent's turn without a report and removes it for good' (expects the dropped text); 'the user's close tells main how many of its messages waiting for the subagent it dropped' (expects dropped=1). ## Wave 3: MCP client
- Config files and keys row 5 (partial; closes the wave-3 hold, MCP owner now holds src/core/mcp). Files: src/core/mcp/workspace_config.zig (readFile kept for the App stamp, projectRoot, load, loadWithEnvironment, trustedByEnvironment, loadLayer, anchorStdioCwd, dropShadowed, containsConfigName, absorb), src/core/mcp/project_config.zig (mergeNative, indexOfConfigName). Change: three layers. Layer 1 is the user file, merged by the profile path. Layer 2 is the git root .mcp.json (projectRoot walks up from the workspace to the nearest .git, else the workspace). Layer 3 is <workspace>/.kimi-code/mcp.json. Layer 3 replaces layer 2 by name, and a stdio server from layer 2 gets cwd = git root when it sets none. Project entries are admitted through the existing per-server admission; the trust grant is enable_all, set when KIMI_CODE_TRUST_WORKSPACE is 1, true, yes or on (trimmed, case-insensitive). A rejected entry stays rejected. decided by parity: layer order and later-wins-by-name (app/mcpConfig/configLoader.ts:28-30, loop at :72-75); git root from cwd (configLoader.ts:25, app/git/workTree.ts findGitWorkTree); stdio cwd default to the git root for the root layer only (configLoader.ts:63, normalizeStdioCwd at :160-164); project layers load only when trusted (workspaceMcpConfigService.ts:130, :165, :243); trusted is requireTrust off, env KIMI_CODE_TRUST_WORKSPACE, or persisted trust (workspaceTrust/workspaceTrustStore.ts:79; trustEnv.ts:3-8). decided by parity: the profile entry of a project name is replaced only by an approved project entry (mergeNative), because Kimi never loads an untrusted project server, so a pending or rejected one must not shadow the user server. Kimi is silent on fx per-server approval (matrix row 4); it stays as an extra grant, and a pending entry stays listed as waiting_for_approval while it does not load. Breaks: a project entry approved under the same name as a profile entry now replaces it (was: profile wins). A nested workspace now reads the git root .mcp.json as well as its own. Root-layer stdio servers run from the git root (was: process cwd). KIMI_CODE_TRUST_WORKSPACE now approves every pending project server for the process. A malformed .kimi-code/mcp.json adds invalid_json and keeps the other layers. Witness (red before, green after): "project layers merge the git root .mcp.json under the cwd .kimi-code/mcp.json by name", "stdio servers from the git root .mcp.json run from the git root", "project root is the nearest ancestor holding .git", "project servers stay pending without trust and the trust env approves them", "the trust env does not lift a rejected project server", "a malformed .kimi-code/mcp.json reports a diagnostic and keeps the root layer", "native merge keeps the profile entry when the project entry is not approved", "native merge lets an approved project entry replace the profile entry of the same name" (replaces "native merge keeps the primary whole entry").
- Config files and keys row 5, held parts (class b and c, named). (b) Persisted workspace trust record: Kimi workspaceTrust/workspaceTrustStore.ts and trustRecord.ts; fx has no trust store, so a repo cannot be trusted by a stored decision. (c) [workspace] require_trust: the config worker must pass the parsed value (src/core/config/kimi_sections.zig workspace_require_trust) into loadWithEnvironment; until then requireTrust off is not honored and the gate is the env switch plus per-server approval. (c) Trust prompt: tui/components/dialogs/trust-prompt.ts belongs to the App surface. (c) Defect for the App owner: src/core/app/app_mcp_runtime.zig:43 stamps only readFile (<workspace_root>/.mcp.json), so edits to the git-root .mcp.json or to .kimi-code/mcp.json do not trigger a reload; the App surface must stamp both project layers. Not run: no zig build or test in this phase; every witness above is unverified until Phase B. tests/e2e/mcp-*.test.ts were not checked for the new precedence or stdio cwd.

## Wave 3: Built-in tools ReadMediaFile
- Built-in tools row 10 (partial). Files: src/core/image/png_crop.zig (new), src/tools/filesystem/read_media_file.zig. Change: region crop for PNG. png_crop.zig decodes non-interlaced 8-bit and 16-bit PNG (gray, gray+alpha, RGB, RGBA, palette): the IDAT stream is inflated with std.compress.flate (zlib) and unfiltered row by row for all five filter types, stopping at the region's last row. The region is clipped to the image edge: a start outside the image fails, a size past the edge is cut (decided by parity: Kimi packages/agent-core-v2/src/agent/media/image-compress.ts:466-500). The crop is re-encoded as PNG with std flate deflate at level 9 (Kimi image-compress.ts deflateLevel 9), filter 0, and the chunks between IHDR and IDAT (PLTE, tRNS, gAMA, iCCP and others) are copied verbatim. ReadMediaFile attaches the crop as image/png, its text naming the applied region. A crop source over 64 MiB is refused (decided by parity: image-compress.ts:58 MAX_IMAGE_DECODE_BYTES). A crop over 8000 px a side or 5 MiB encoded is refused (fx attach limits). Breaks: imageResult takes its text and a covers_full_file flag (internal). Stale text sits in tools.zig, see the defect below. Witness (not run in Phase A; tests written and read, to run in Phase B): png_crop.zig "png crop keeps the requested rgb region pixels", "png crop unfilters every filter type back to the source pixels", "png crop handles grayscale, gray alpha and 16-bit samples", "png crop keeps a palette image and copies its PLTE chunk", "png crop writes a PNG of the region size", "png crop rejects a region outside the image bounds", "png crop clips a region that runs past the image edge", "png crop rejects interlaced and sub-byte depth PNGs", "png crop rejects bytes that are not a PNG and a truncated file"; read_media_file.zig "ReadMediaFile crops a PNG region and attaches the crop", "ReadMediaFile rejects a region that starts outside the image", "ReadMediaFile names the gap for a region on a JPEG, WebP or GIF"; "ReadMediaFile decodes path, region and full_resolution" unchanged.
- Built-in tools row 10 gap, JPEG and WebP region crops (class (b)). Cause: Zig 0.17 std (/config/tools/zig-0.17.0/lib/std) has flate, zstd, lzma, xz and base64 but no JPEG or WebP codec (grep for jpeg, webp and gif finds none), and fx has no image pixel decoder (core/images/image_data.zig reads header dimensions only). Kimi crops them (image-compress.ts:60 RECODABLE_MIME). A region on them fails with the gap message; a plain read still attaches them. GIF is not cropped by Kimi either.
- Built-in tools row 10 gap, video (class (b)). Cause: std has no demuxer (grep for matroska, mp4, webm and ebml finds none) and fx has no video frame sampler. Video stays refused; Kimi also refuses region and full_resolution on video (readMediaFileTool.ts:275).
- Built-in tools row 10 gap, PNG with bit depth 1, 2 or 4 and interlaced (Adam7) PNG (class (b)). Cause: png_crop.zig does not unpack sub-byte pixels or walk the seven Adam7 passes; those files fail with the unsupported message. Kimi decodes them through decodeToJimp, so this is an fx gap.
- DEFECT (cause: tools.zig belongs to the registry worker, not edited here): read_media_file_description (src/builtins/tools.zig:57) says region cropping is not supported and fails, and the region property text (src/builtins/tools.zig:284) says cropping is not available yet. Both are stale once this commit lands; the registry worker must update them.
- Not run: Phase A has no zig build or zig test. Std APIs used (flate.Decompress.init, flate.Compress.init with .best, std.Io.Reader.fixed, readSliceAll, takeByte, Writer.Allocating, base64 Decoder.calcSizeForSlice) were checked by reading lib/std source.

## Correction: 6d03f24d cron journal persistence
- Cron journal persist (correction to 6d03f24d). Status: coded. Files: src/main.zig. Change: 6d03f24d reported "Cron journal persists across restarts", but it only landed Session.appendCronJournal and Session.cronJournalLines in src/core/session/session_adapter.zig. Two parts were incomplete: (1) App.persistCronLine in src/main.zig was an empty body, so drained cron lines were never written; (2) cron_drive.replayJournal was never called at startup, so journaled tasks were not reloaded after a restart. This commit completes both. persistCronLine appends each line to the active session through appendCronJournal, and App.tickCron calls restoreCronJournalOnce before its first tick, which replays the active session journal into the cron runtime once per session id. Breaks: none. Witness: none added in Phase A (no test was written and nothing was compiled or run); a restore test needs an App fixture and is still to be written. Gaps: lines drained while no session is open are dropped (non-durable mode); replay stops at the first invalid record, while the Kimi cron store (refs/kimi-code/apps/vis/server/src/lib/cron-store.ts listCronTasks) skips records that fail validation. src/main.zig is in the config worker wave-3 ownership; it was edited here under this task explicit owned-path grant.

## Gap: cron journal lines drained with no open session
- Cron journal (surface: Built-in tools, cron rows 21 to 23). Files: src/main.zig (persistCronLine). Gap: a cron line drained when no session is open has no session journal to append to, so persistCronLine drops it. Cause: the journal is per session and the drain runs before a session is opened. Owner: session surface and main.zig. Witness needed (Phase B): a test that drains a line with no open session and then opens one, expecting the line to be kept; this test does not exist yet, and the current behaviour is the drop.

## Wave 3: Permission classifier tests removed by bf9f6f34
- Scope: bf9f6f34 removed 33 test blocks from src/core/permissions and src/core/tooling/tool_admission.zig, not sixteen as the brief stated. Each one is decided below. Outcome: restored 1, replaced 16, removed by Kimi semantics with no replacement 16. Witnesses were verified by reading the bodies, not run. Code is unchanged in this commit.
- Permission classifier restored (verbatim, already in the tree): "configured allow remains authoritative for a destructive command" (src/core/tooling/tool_admission.zig:4277). The body is byte-identical to bf9f6f34^ (cmp). Under Kimi, auto approves before user-configured allow and ask (permissionPolicyService.ts:45 against :47 and :48), so the auto-mode configured-rule result stays the same.
- Permission classifier replaced: "decide allows irreversible invocation in yolo mode without consulting a decider" (old permission_gate.zig). Replacement: "yolo mode approves a reversible write without a decider" and "yolo mode denies an irreversible invocation without a decider" (src/core/permissions/permission_gate.zig:189 and :197). They check that yolo does not bypass the irreversible gate. Kimi asks for dangerous commands under yolo (dangerous-command-ask.ts:141-142), and yolo approves only after that (yolo-mode-approve.ts:15).
- Permission classifier replaced: "permissionModeLabel maps active permission mode labels" (old permissions.zig). Replacement: "permissionModeLabel maps Kimi permission mode labels" (src/core/permissions/permissions.zig:1930). It checks labels manual, yolo, auto and display labels Always Ask, Ask When Needed, Never Ask. Kimi: types.ts:6 and apps/kimi-code/src/tui/utils/permission-mode.ts:4-6.
- Permission classifier replaced: "file target evaluator requires approval for unconfigured external target in auto mode" (old permissions.zig). The auto half is removed by Kimi (auto-mode-approve.ts:15, service order permissionPolicyService.ts:45 before the sensitive-file ask at :49). Replacement for the prompt witness: "file target evaluator requires approval for unconfigured external target in ask mode" (src/core/permissions/permissions.zig:3246). It checks the same external target with mode ask and asserts prompt_required.
- Permission classifier removed by Kimi, no replacement: "direct git push branch proof accepts only explicit literal operands". The helper directGitPushBranch was deleted by bf9f6f34. Its only caller was provenBindingsForAction (old tool_admission.zig:826), which fed the auto reviewer proven bindings. Kimi has no reviewer: auto approves everything except deny (auto-mode-approve.ts:15; permissionPolicyService.ts:40-45).
- Permission classifier replaced: "automatic terminal admission reviews only sensitive typed input". Replacement: "automatic terminal admission approves typed input and keeps configured denies" (src/core/tooling/tool_admission.zig:3699). It checks that auto approves typed terminal input with no classifier call, that configured deny gives policy_denied under auto, and that a configured ask prompts under yolo and ask.
- Permission classifier replaced: "ask-only policy bypasses prompt and reviewer in auto and uses the ordinary prompt in ask". Replacement: "ask-only policy bypasses prompt in auto and yolo and uses the ordinary prompt in ask" (tool_admission.zig:3620). It checks auto and yolo approve without a prompt or classifier call, and ask prompts once.
- Permission classifier replaced: "yolo admission bypasses policy prompts and review after structural validation". Replacement: "yolo admission approves routine commands and keeps configured denies" (tool_admission.zig:3810). It checks yolo approves with source yolo and no prompt or classifier call, configured deny gives policy_denied with no prompt, and malformed JSON returns UnexpectedEndOfInput.
- Permission classifier replaced: "yolo file admission preserves canonical mutation authority". Replacement: "yolo file admission approves reversible writes and keeps configured denies" (tool_admission.zig:3881). It checks the file_mutation authority carries the canonical target path, at least two policy targets, and an expected identity on the second.
- Permission classifier replaced: "automatic destructive command reaches reviewer without human prompter". Replacement: "auto approves dangerous commands without asking while yolo asks for them" (tool_admission.zig:4226). Auto approves sudo rm -rf with source auto_mode and no prompt. Yolo asks once for the same command. Kimi: dangerous-command-ask.ts:131 skips auto, and :141-142 asks under yolo.
- Permission classifier replaced: "configured command authority skips automatic review". Replacement: "configured command authority is used before auto authority" (tool_admission.zig:4317).
- Permission classifier replaced: "automatic clean direct command bypasses the reviewer". Replacement: "automatic clean direct command stays direct without a reviewer" (tool_admission.zig:4388). Checks zero classifier calls and the direct_only fingerprint.
- Permission classifier replaced: "automatic clean TTY command requires reviewed shell authority". Replacement: "automatic clean TTY command runs with auto shell authority" (tool_admission.zig:4429). Checks source auto_mode and zero classifier calls.
- Permission classifier replaced: "routine commands that a user alias or function redefines go to review". Replacement: "routine commands that a user alias or function redefines run with auto authority" (tool_admission.zig:4587). Checks source auto_mode and zero classifier calls.
- Permission classifier replaced: "routine commands go to review while the snapshot has fallen back". Replacement: "routine commands run with auto authority while the snapshot has fallen back" (tool_admission.zig:4636). Checks source auto_mode and zero classifier calls.
- Permission classifier replaced: "known reversible auto commands bypass the reviewer". Replacement: "auto commands run with auto authority without a reviewer" (tool_admission.zig:4667). Checks once, source auto_mode, and zero classifier calls.
- Permission classifier replaced in part: "external prepared file review carries frozen path and diff authority". The path and identity half is covered by "yolo file admission approves reversible writes and keeps configured denies" (tool_admission.zig:3881). The approval-without-packet half is covered by "auto external file write is approved without a reviewer packet" (tool_admission.zig:4960). The diff-review half is removed by Kimi (no review packet; auto-mode-approve.ts:15).
- Permission classifier replaced in part: "automatic added-root write bypasses reviewer while untrusted external write does not". Replacement: "auto writes to added and external roots are approved without a reviewer" (tool_admission.zig:5115). Checks zero classifier calls and file_mutation authority. The untrusted-external prompt half is removed by Kimi: auto approves every write (auto-mode-approve.ts:15).
- Permission classifier removed by Kimi, no replacement (review or reviewer-only behaviour; Kimi auto never reviews, auto-mode-approve.ts:15, service order permissionPolicyService.ts:40-45):
  - "automatic non-allow is recoverable regardless tool approval policy"
  - "automatic review trace preserves the typed unavailable cause without action text"
  - "automatic admission honors reviewer clear when command appears in tool output"
  - "missing contextual review authority maps to unavailable without reviewer transport"
  - "automatic review receives exact command and mints matching one-call authority"
  - "automatic review includes only matching host-proven branch for direct git push"
  - "delegated command effects remain reviewer owned"
  - "automatic reviewer caution returns a recoverable hold without a prompter"
  - "invalid automatic review returns to the agent before prompting"
  - "invalid automatic review returns a recoverable denial without a prompter"
  - "exhausted review transport preserves deterministic auto lanes"
  - "built-in structured review sends exact arguments without redundant schema"
  - "selected dynamic MCP review receives exact arguments and advertised schema"
  - "automatic trusted-root write keeps persistence targets on reviewer path": Kimi auto approves before sensitive-file ask (permissionPolicyService.ts:45, :49).
  - "automatic trusted-root overwrite preserves configured read disclosure review": Kimi auto approves before user-configured ask (permissionPolicyService.ts:45, :47).
- Defect (open, not fixed in Phase A): permission_gate.zig yolo irreversible with no decider is denied (test at :197). Kimi drops the dangerous-command ask entirely when nonInteractive (permissionPolicyService.ts:42-44), so Kimi non-interactive yolo approves the same command. Cause: fx treats the missing decider as a deny. Owner: permissions surface, with the CLI worker for the non-interactive flag. Phase B witness needed: a non-interactive yolo test that expects allow.
- Defect (open): the count in the brief (sixteen) does not match bf9f6f34 (33 test blocks). Cause: the brief count was wrong; all 33 are decided here.

## Wave 3: MCP trust prompt gate and trust record modes
- Matrix 05 MCP client row 8 (coded: startup gate and non-TUI prompt; TUI rendering and the call site are open defects below). Files: src/core/app/app_mcp_runtime.zig (TrustPrompt, startupTrustGate, hasProjectLayer, stdinTrustPrompt, chooseOnStdin, parseTrustAnswer, tests), src/core/mcp/workspace_trust.zig (trust_dir_permissions, trust_record_permissions, writePrivateRecord, grant). Change: startupTrustGate continues without prompting unless a project MCP layer exists (root .mcp.json or .kimi-code/mcp.json) and promptRequired is true; a null prompt (no TTY) continues with project layers gated, as Kimi print mode does (apps/kimi-code/src/cli/v2/run-v2-print.ts:273-279); otherwise the choice goes through applyPromptChoice with io_mod.milliTimestamp(). The project-layer condition is the owner's instruction for this task. Kimi prompts for every untrusted folder (apps/kimi-code/src/tui/kimi-tui.ts:5033-5090), so this is a narrowing to confirm, not a parity claim. Non-TUI prompt: Enter, t, trust, y or yes trusts (Enter is the highlighted Trust and continue, apps/kimi-code/src/tui/components/dialogs/trust-prompt.ts:27-35); any other answer, or end of input, exits (decided by parity: kimi-tui.ts:5033-5090, a non-trust choice stops the program). Trust record: the directory is created with Permissions.fromMode(0o700) through Dir.createDirPathStatus; the record is written to a temp file created with Permissions.fromMode(0o600) through createFileAbsolute, synced, and renamed into place; io.e2eFailIfDurableMutationAttempted is kept at the write. Kimi: FileStorageService(homeDir, 0o700, 0o600) (packages/agent-core-v2/src/app/bootstrap/bootstrap.ts:153). Breaks: none; no existing signature changes, and workspace_trust.zig no longer calls io_mod.makeDirRecursive or io_mod.writeFileAtomic. Witness (red before, green after): "the trust record is 0600 and its directory 0700", "the startup trust gate prompts only for an untrusted project layer and acts on the choice", "the stdin trust answer trusts on Enter, t or yes and exits otherwise". Unverified: nothing compiled or run in Phase A.
- Matrix 05 MCP client row 8 defect (open, class c, owner: TUI surface). Trust prompt rendering is absent. Cause: fx's TUI has no modal or blocking dialog component (grep for dialog and activeDialog under src finds nothing), so Kimi's TrustPromptComponent (apps/kimi-code/src/tui/kimi-tui.ts:5062-5070) has no fx component to mount into. The stdin prompt is the non-TUI path until a TUI owner adds one.
- Matrix 05 MCP client row 8 defect (open, class c, owner: config worker: src/main.zig, app_lifecycle.zig, app_bootstrap_runtime.zig). startupTrustGate has no caller. Cause: the only startup MCP load is App.loadMcpHost (src/main.zig:1805), outside this surface. The caller must pass env_trusted from KIMI_CODE_TRUST_WORKSPACE (workspace_config.zig trustedByEnvironment is private, so it needs a pub wrapper there), pass stdinTrustPrompt() only when stdin is a TTY and null otherwise, call startupTrustGate before loadMcpHost, and stop the program on exit_program.
- Wave 3 MCP config defect "trust record modes" (open, shared io) is closed by this commit: the record and its directory are created 0600 and 0700 in workspace_trust.zig, so src/core/shared/io.zig is not changed.

## Wave 3: TowerSpawn
- Built-in tools row 31 (coded, partial). Files: src/core/tower/spawn.zig (new: Kind, parseKind, WorkerBriefing and workerPrompt, ReviewerBriefing and reviewerPrompt), src/tools/tower/spawn.zig (new: TowerSpawn spec, validateArgs, spawnWith, run with roster, mission owner, saveRendered and appendLog), src/tools/tower/index.zig (exports spawn, specs and names gain TowerSpawn), src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig (Runtime.launchTowerChild: a background message from the root through executeManaged with the coder profile). Change: TowerSpawn validates name, kind and mission or review target, refuses a terminal mission, creates or reuses the mission worktree, builds the Kimi worker or reviewer briefing, launches through launchTowerChild, then records the roster entry, the mission owner and the spawn log. It requires approval. With no subagent runtime in the dispatch context it refuses before any side effect. Breaks: index specs grow from 12 to 13 names (the registry must count TowerSpawn); tool_host.zig gains one pub function and changes no existing signature. Witness (new, red before, green after, not run in Phase A): "Tower spawn kinds are worker and reviewer only", "Tower worker prompt names the worktree, branch, scope and mission", "Tower survey prompt is read-only and has no worker completion step", "Tower reviewer prompt carries the target, base and the checklist for the kind of review", "TowerSpawn refuses unknown keys, a missing name and a missing kind", "TowerSpawn validates the kind and the kind's required field", "TowerSpawn refuses a blank or padded agent name", "TowerSpawn refuses with the not-initialized message when tower is absent", "TowerSpawn needs approval and is reversible"; changed: "Tower index exports one spec per tool name in order" (names extended).
- decided by parity: the child's first message carries the mission file, worktree path, branch, scope and the worker completion steps (Kimi features/tower/tools/spawn/spawnTool.ts:456-520 buildPrompt). Kimi silent on the child profile name in fx terms, so the child runs the default coder profile (Kimi TOWER_WORKER_PROFILE, spawnTool.ts:410, not present in fx).
- decided by parity: a worker spawn whose worktree cannot be set up continues with a warning note (spawnTool.ts:252); a terminal mission (merged or abandoned) refuses with no worktree or agent created (spawnTool.ts:193); a worker spawn records the mission owner as the agent name (spawnTool.ts:327); the child is registered only after launch succeeds (spawnTool.ts:314).
- Defect (open, class c, owner: registry worker, src/core/tooling/tool_dispatch.zig): TowerSpawn cannot reach the subagent runtime from dispatch. Cause: DispatchContext (tool_dispatch.zig:250) has no subagent host or ExecuteOptions field, so call() refuses with host_unavailable_message. Fix: the tower dispatch passes a Launch to spawnWith. Row 31 stays partial until then.
- Defect (open, class c, owner: profiles surface, src/core/profiles/profiles.zig): fx has no tower worker profile, so the child runs the coder profile where Kimi runs TOWER_WORKER_PROFILE (spawnTool.ts:410).
- Defect (open, class c, owner: permissions and subagent authority, src/core/subagent/authority.zig): Kimi sets the child permission mode to auto (spawnTool.ts:422). fx's launch inherits the parent mode through ExecuteOptions.parent_permission_mode.
- Defect (open, class c, owner: permissions worker): Kimi hard-denies Write and Edit outside the worktree for a tower child (spawnTool.ts buildPrompt workplace text). fx has no per-child write root, so the briefing is advisory only.
- Defect (open): the spawn-base snapshot is not ported. Kimi commits the base checkout's uncommitted changes as the branch's first commit (spawnTool.ts:232-256, store.addWorktree). Cause: src/core/tower has no addWorktree or snapshot commit path.
- Defect (open): the previous-worker history, the review-request scan and the reviewer history sections are not ported (spawnTool.ts workerHistorySection, reviewHistorySection, findReviewRequest). Cause: store has reviewsFor but no latestReview and no review-request scan.
- Defect (open): the reviewer base is state.base, where Kimi uses store.diffBase of the reviewed mission (spawnTool.ts buildPrompt). Cause: fx has no diffBase.
- Defect (open): the model alias "primary" is not resolved (Kimi configSection resolveSubagentBindingWithPrimary). The raw model string goes to executeManaged.
- Defect (open): the roster agentId is the agent name. Cause: tool_host generates the child id during admission and ManagedExecutionResult does not return it.
- Defect (open): no branch lease (Kimi withBranchLease, spawnTool.ts:232) and no spawn rate limit (Kimi towerRateLimit service). Cause: fx has neither.
- Defect (open, row 35): the worker completion step the prompt asks for (TowerComplete) refuses every caller, because fx has no worker identity (store.zig complete_caller_message).
- Defect (open risk): the roster save happens after launch. A save failure then leaves a running child that is not registered. Kimi has the same order (spawnTool.ts:314), so it is recorded rather than changed.
- Test gap (open): launchTowerChild has no test here, since tool_host tests belong to the later worker. Wanted witness: launchTowerChild sends a background message from the root with the coder profile.

## Wave 3 addendum 2: permission classifier tests removed by bf9f6f34
- Supersedes the "removed by Kimi, no replacement" list above. All 33 test blocks removed by bf9f6f34 are now decided: restored 1, replaced 32. Each replacement is a named test with the Kimi rule that makes its outcome the new behaviour. Witnesses were verified by reading the bodies and the admission code, not run.
- Restored verbatim (identical body to bf9f6f34^, cmp-checked): "configured allow remains authoritative for a destructive command" (src/core/tooling/tool_admission.zig, existing test).
- Replaced, reviewer and classifier tests. The new tests are at the end of src/core/tooling/tool_admission.zig. Kimi: auto approves before any reviewer or configured ask (auto-mode-approve.ts:15; permissionPolicyService.ts:45, configured ask at :47, sensitive-file ask at :49).
  - "automatic non-allow is recoverable regardless tool approval policy" -> "auto approves a command a reviewer would hold and ignores classifier output". Checks once, denial_reason null, execution authority present, zero classifier calls. Not kept: the review_caution denial and its rationale text, which have no Kimi counterpart.
  - "automatic review trace preserves the typed unavailable cause without action text" -> same test (invalid-review case). Checks no denial reason is produced under auto. Not kept: the review_unavailable typed cause.
  - "automatic admission honors reviewer clear when command appears in tool output" -> same test. Checks the assertions this old test made after clearance (decision once, denial null, authority non-null) and that the classifier is not called. Not kept: the reviewer clear and the prior-trace input.
  - "missing contextual review authority maps to unavailable without reviewer transport" -> "auto approves ordinary commands without review authority or budget" (permission_review_turn null case). Checks once with auto_mode authority and zero classifier calls.
  - "automatic review receives exact command and mints matching one-call authority" -> existing "auto commands run with auto authority without a reviewer" (src/core/tooling/tool_admission.zig:4667). Checks once with auto_mode one-call authority and zero classifier calls. Not kept: the command sent to the reviewer.
  - "automatic review includes only matching host-proven branch for direct git push" -> "auto git push runs with auto authority without a branch proof". Checks git push under auto returns once with auto_mode authority and zero classifier calls.
  - "direct git push branch proof accepts only explicit literal operands" -> same git push test. The helper directGitPushBranch is deleted; its only caller was the reviewer's proven-bindings path (old tool_admission.zig:826). Not kept: literal-operand parsing.
  - "delegated command effects remain reviewer owned" -> "auto approves delegated and compound shell commands without a classifier call" (git-free subset: rtk rm, comment-with-rm, heredoc, rm variants, rm with redirect). Checks once, denial null, zero classifier calls. Not covered: the old git subset (checkout, switch, pull, clean, reset) is not in the new test.
  - "automatic reviewer caution returns a recoverable hold without a prompter" -> "auto approves a command a reviewer would hold and ignores classifier output" (caution case). Checks once, zero classifier calls.
  - "invalid automatic review returns to the agent before prompting" -> same test (invalid case). Checks once, zero classifier calls.
  - "invalid automatic review returns a recoverable denial without a prompter" -> same test (invalid case). Checks no denial and zero classifier calls.
  - "exhausted review transport preserves deterministic auto lanes" -> "auto approves ordinary commands without review authority or budget" (exhausted budget case, the command the old test denied). Checks once, denial null, auto_mode authority, zero classifier calls.

  - "selected dynamic MCP review receives exact arguments and advertised schema" -> "auto approves an advertised dynamic MCP call without a review payload". Checks once, execution authority present, zero classifier calls, and no arguments or schema sent. Not kept: the payload.

Checks once, file_mutation authority for each, zero reviewer calls. Kimi: sensitive-file ask (permissionPolicyService.ts:49) is after auto approve (:45).
  - "automatic trusted-root overwrite preserves configured read disclosure review" -> "auto overwrite of a read-denied file is approved without a reviewer" (same setup, read_file deny rule). Checks once, denial null, zero reviewer calls. Kimi: user-configured ask (:47) is after auto approve (:45), and the rule is for read_file only.

## Wave 3 addendum 3: dead classifier defect
- Kimi check (correction to the premise): dangerous-command-ask.ts:131 returns undefined only under auto, so the dangerous-command guard runs under manual and yolo, not only yolo. It asks for dangerous commands (:141-142) in both, and yolo lets non-dangerous unanalyzable commands pass (:144). fx manual asks for every approval-required command, so the observable behaviour matches. Auto skips the guard and approves (auto-mode-approve.ts:15).
- Kimi has no LLM classifier or reviewer. Auto is rule-based (auto-mode-approve.ts:15), and permissionPolicyService.ts:40-54 has no reviewer policy. The classifier therefore has no Kimi equivalent, and its end state is deletion.
- Guard wiring (already in admission, verified by reading): tool_admission.zig defaultRunCommandPermissionOutcome (yolo branch) calls command_admission.dangerousShellCommand (src/core/permissions/command_admission.zig, dangerousInvocation). Witness added at the end of src/core/tooling/tool_admission.zig: "Kimi dangerous commands prompt in ask and yolo and run without a prompt in auto". It covers sudo rm -rf, env plus nested sh -c shutdown, dd to a disk, systemctl poweroff, and mkfs.ext4. Each command makes no prompt under auto, one prompt under yolo, and one prompt under ask. Witness verified by reading, not run.
- Dead classifier: NOT deleted in this pass. ## Wave 3: Skills and discovery (rows 2, 4, 27)
This section supersedes the held rows 2, 4 and 27 in the second pass above. Phase A: nothing below was built or run; witnesses are new or changed tests not yet executed. Matrix rows 2, 4 and 27 in docs/kimi-parity-matrix.md are not updated here because that file is not an owned path.
- Skills and discovery row 2 (coded). Files: src/core/skills/skill_contract.zig (SkillForm, Skill.form, resolveSkillMetadata, resolveFlatMetadata, skillFileStem), src/core/skills/skill_runtime.zig (collectSkillEntries, appendSkillsFromOpenDir, appendFlatSkillCandidate, appendInspectedSkill, directoryFormExists, openPrimarySkillFileNamed, openValidatedSkillCandidate, loadKnownSkill, statKnownSkill, hashSkillDirectory, OpenedSkillCandidate.openResource), src/core/skills/skill_invocation.zig (two metadata re-checks use the skill form). Change: a top-level <name>.md in a skills root is a skill named by its file stem, unless its frontmatter names it. A directory skill with the same stem (<name>/SKILL.md as a file) wins and the flat file is skipped. Flat files are read only at the root depth. A flat skill opens and revalidates its own file, and its resource reads are limited to that file, so sibling files are refused through the skill tool. Scan order is directory candidates, then flat files, then recursion. Decided by parity: stem naming and frontmatter override (Kimi parser.ts:95); directory form wins on a clash (Kimi fileSkillDiscovery.ts:115); scan order (Kimi fileSkillDiscovery.ts:96-139). Breaks: a top-level .md in ~/.fx/skills, ~/.agents/skills or a project skills root now loads as a skill; a top-level skill now beats a same-named skill nested below it (Kimi order); symlinked non-directory entries under a root with an authority are skipped silently, where they were reported as linked_candidate_unavailable. Defects: (1) flat skills cannot read sibling files through the skill tool; Kimi lets the model read them with its file tools (fx stricter, as row 30). Cause: fx resource reads are contained to the skill's own directory, and a flat skill's directory is the shared root. (2) Flat symlinked files load only under a symlink authority. Cause: the fx symlink containment policy (rows 15 and 30). ## Wave 3: Tool-host tests deleted by 8ecc4433
- Subagents tool-host row (coded as replacements; none restored). Reason: reject semantics removed the queue, the wait-and-run order and the dropped count, so no deleted test's behaviour still exists. Replacements (all in src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig):
  - "a message to a busy subagent waits and runs as its next work, in order" -> "a parent's message to a running subagent is refused, and a failed turn does not carry it forward". Checks the parent's message to a busy child is refused with child_already_running and the failed turn does not carry it forward. The old test checked queued messages ran in order.
  - "a message past a busy subagent's full queue is refused to its sender" -> "a parent's message to a running subagent is refused, and a failed turn does not carry it forward". Checks the refusal to the sender; the full-queue condition no longer exists, so every message to a busy child is refused.
  - "a user's stop drops the parent's messages waiting for a subagent, and its report says how many" -> "a user's stop of a work that owes no report posts no report, and a message sent while it ran is refused". Checks nothing waits to be dropped (user_dropped stays empty) and no report is posted.
  - "messages waiting for a busy subagent are taken into its next turn as one work" -> "a parent's message while the user's turn runs is refused, and nothing waits to start when the turn ends". Checks nothing waiting starts after the turn.
  - "the user's close tells main how many of its messages waiting for the subagent it dropped" -> "the user's close of a working subagent reports that the user closed it". Checks the close report says the user closed it, with cause user_close; the dropped count no longer exists.

- Gate runner (changed). Files: scripts/unit-test-gate.sh (new). Change: the local unit-test gate is now `scripts/unit-test-gate.sh <logfile>`. It takes /tmp/fx-build.lock, runs `zig build install-test` (build.zig install-test step, binary zig-out/bin/fx-test), then runs the binary in terminal mode without --listen under `timeout 1200`. It prints BUILD_EXIT, TEST_EXIT and the FAIL/panic/passed lines. Reason: `zig build test` runs its test binary in listen mode; a test panic in listen mode leaves the binary blocked on a futex, and the process holds /tmp/fx-build.lock, so every queued build deadlocked (observed: pid 3614817 and two relaunched test binaries, all holding the lock). The wrapper cannot hold the lock beyond its timeout.
- Conflict left open for the owner: AGENTS.md (supported gate is `zig build test` in listen mode) and .github ci.yml still use the listen-mode command. This change applies to the local and agent runner only. Decision needed: whether CI and AGENTS.md move to scripts/unit-test-gate.sh.
- Witness: the gate output of the wrapper, quoted in the final report of the Phase B run.

## Phase B repair: skills

Cause: the test temp dirs live under /workspace/fx/fx/.zig-cache/tmp, inside this git repo. findProjectRoot (src/core/skills/skill_runtime.zig, mirroring Kimi skillRoots.ts findProjectRoot, nearest .git ancestor) therefore resolved the project root to /workspace/fx/fx, so workspace-relative roots (.agents, .codex, custom-skills, symlinked ancestors) were looked up in the repo root and nothing was found. Fix: each affected test creates a .git marker at its workspace root, so the project root is the test workspace as it is for a user outside git.

Fixed tests (cause and fix):

- skill discovery rejects symlinked ancestors inside an automatic root: marker home/workspace/.git (the .agents symlink is only reached when the workspace is the project root).
- skill discovery reports a symlinked automatic root whose target lacks the trailing component: marker home/workspace/.git.

## Phase B repair: session cron journal

Test: core.session.session_adapter.test "cron journal lines persist as session items and read back in order".

Cause: Session.appendCronJournal wrote cron_journal items with no turn open. The session manager (src/core/session_manager/fold.zig plan) accepts an item only inside an open turn, so the write failed with InvalidTransition.

Fix: appendCronJournal (src/core/session/session_adapter.zig) opens a turn in the same batch when none is open (turn_started, the items, turn_committed), and writes items straight into the open turn otherwise. The cron-only turn produces no conversation turn on replay (turn_committed is ignored and only conversation turns reach sink.turn), so turn_numbers stays consistent after restore.

Verification: scripts/unit-test-gate.sh (log /tmp/phaseb-repair-gate.log) printed "2383/11044 core.session.session_adapter.test.cron journal lines persist as session items and read back in order...OK".

Gap: a cron line drained while no session is open is still dropped (the no-session gap above); its witness test is not written here.

## Phase B repair: mcp_host withdrawn answer

- Not fixed, production code and test unchanged. core.mcp_host.runtime.test "an answer to a withdrawn 2025 question reaches no one, and the next question gets its own" (runtime.zig, HEAD line 2477). The engine gates elicitation on that same string: src/mcp/server.zig:212 `elicitation.declared(options.client.capabilities)`, and src/mcp/protocol/mrtr.zig `supported()` returns false when no elicitation key is present. `options.questions` is now read nowhere (runtime.zig:143 is the only mention). So every form elicitation is rejected with invalid_params (src/mcp/core/elicitation.zig `.reject`, src/mcp/server.zig reject path) before the runtime sees it, and the ask callback is never called. Test 3636 "a question no call can show is answered cancel" fails by the same mechanism (`c1=` instead of `c1=cancel`).
- Why no fix in scope: the test expects in-app answering of form elicitation when the host sets questions = .form. The recorded decision (commit 38e049c5; "Wave 3: MCP client" entry above; docs/kimi-parity-matrix.md row 20) is that the client does not declare elicitation, and the witness test "MCP client declares no elicitation, sampling, or roots capability" pins "{}". Restoring a working answer path needs one of two changes, both outside this scope. (a) Advertise elicitation: contradicts that decision and the witness test. (b) Decouple the engine's accepted-form gate from the advertised capabilities, in src/mcp/server.zig and src/mcp/engine.zig. The ledger holds elicitation-handler removal for an owner decision, and this change would re-enable elicitation.
- Owner decision needed: should a host with questions = .form still answer unsolicited form elicitation while the client advertises none? The "Wave 3: MCP client" entry says fx still does. HEAD does not, because the engine gate reads only the advertised "{}". Until that is decided, the test stays red and its expectation stays as written.

## Phase B repair: tool_runtime

- "request tool permission honors configured deny and allow rules" (tool_runtime.zig, the hang at gate test 4575). Cause: TestRuntime defaulted to interactive = true, so the worker prompter was installed; the "*" ask rule outranks the "read" allow rule under deny > ask > allow (commit 9a3f3574, Kimi policy order), so the read call prompted and no responder answered, parking the binary in futex_do_wait. Production is correct for an interactive host, so the fix is test setup. Fix: TestRuntime sets interactive = false, as its neighbours do; the ask-over-allow call expects permission_required (was once, stale by 9a3f3574); the allow-only rule set is a new third assertion and expects once, so the allow path stays covered. Test setup changed: yes (interactive = false). Expectation changed: yes (ask outranks allow, Kimi order).
- "run_command default user profile requires configured or auto mode shell authority" (renamed from "...configured or reviewed shell authority"). Cause: auto no longer consults the classifier (bf9f6f34 row 24), so the source is auto_mode and no reviewer call happens. - "file mutation lifecycle decodes each call at most once". Cause: the preflight loop ran every case in auto, and auto never prompts (the "prompted" external new file was expected to prompt). - "file mutation preflight separates edit approval from equality disclosure". Cause: equality_prompt_required is false under auto (preflight: request.permission_mode != .auto), so the read-denied cases returned allowed. - "non-interactive ask denies an external write as permission required without a human prompt" (renamed from "disabled automatic reviewer returns a recoverable denial without a human prompt"). - "configured ask rule prompts the worker". Cause: the test ran in auto, which ignores configured ask rules (bf9f6f34 row 24), so no prompt reached the worker. Fix: TestRuntime and the runPermissionRequest argument use ask. Setup changed: auto to ask. Expectations unchanged.
- "registered terminal exec preserves invalid execution authority error" and the test captured-shell decoder. Cause: decodeTestCapturedShell required action = "run", so the call failed as "invalid captured shell input" before the run_command backend could report InvalidRunCommandExecutionAuthority. Cause: the browser workspace registry registers the tool as shell (browser_workspace_tools.zig) and requires action, so the Bash-named call matched no tool. Fix: name shell with action run. Cause: same as above; the browser host is shell, so the Bash-named call raised NotRunCommand. Fix: name shell with action run in the four calls. Setup changed: arguments. Expectations unchanged.

## Phase B repair: core.goal.state panic

- core.goal.state.test "Pause moves an active goal to paused and rejects a finished one" (state.zig:473): panic "attempt to use null value" at `(try state.markComplete(alloc, 70, null)).?`. Gate /tmp/goal-gate.log: TEST_EXIT=134 at 4645, reproduced on the tree before this entry. Cause: the test completes a goal that is paused. markComplete, markBlocked, recordTurn and recordTokens all go through activeGoal, which returns null unless status is active, so the unwrap of null is the test's own expectation.
- Product decision it conflicts with: a paused goal is completed only after it is resumed. update_goal.zig answers a complete request on a non-active goal with "Goal not completed: no active goal."; reminder.zig paused_template says to call UpdateGoal active before resuming goal-driven work; pause accepts only an active goal (StatusInvalid).
- Provenance: the test and the production code landed together in e5091e0f, and the ledger records that the goal tests were never run (Phase A forbids zig test), so the test was never checked against the code it covers. Kimi goalService.ts is not in this checkout, so Kimi parity for completing a paused goal is unverified.
- Fix: none in production code. The test expectation is stale against the decision above. The test block was not edited (outside scope). Owner action: in that test, call state.resumeGoal before markComplete, or assert error.StatusInvalid or a null completion for a paused goal.

## Goal state panic at 4645: test asserted an unreachable state

- Path: the test called markComplete on a paused goal and unwrapped the result with .?. markComplete returns null for a paused goal by design (activeGoal requires active). update_goal's complete path handles that null and returns "Goal not completed: no active goal." without panicking, so the runtime did not panic.
- Case: the test asserted a state the runtime cannot produce (a completion of a paused goal). Test fixed: the goal is resumed (resumeGoal) before completion. Production unchanged.
- Verified: the gate run /tmp/gate-goal-verify.log prints "4645/11044 core.goal.state.test.Pause moves an active goal to paused and rejects a finished one...OK".
- Row 15 test fixtures (MCP tool names in tests). Files: src/core/mcp_host/model.zig (test blocks only). Synthetic names passed straight to the render helper (mcp_linear_list, mcp_slack_send, mcp_aside_repl) are unchanged, as row 15 states for synthetic dynamic-tool names in Zig unit tests. ## Ledger note: gm next_context leak
For the MCP parity pass: gm's next_context has been returning events from other runs (a run's step reply carried another run's task, a 28 KB event feed, and a job list from unrelated runs). That leak is being fixed by gm, in gm's own repository. This pass does not duplicate it: no fx-side workaround and no change to gm's files.

## Decision record: MCP parity pass

- Scope: fx gets a full MCP server, not an ACP-only path. fx had no MCP server before this pass (src/mcp and src/core/mcp_host are client-only; the only JSON-RPC server is ACP). Surface to build: initialize, resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read, resources/subscribe, resources/unsubscribe, logging/setLevel, completion/complete, plus gm's skill:// and run:// resources. Reason: the owner asked for parity with gm's live MCP server.
- Skill content source: vendored copies of gm's three skill files (gm/SKILL.md, gm/WORKFLOWS.md, gm-continue/SKILL.md), each checked against a pinned sha256 at serve time. Reason: a vendored copy with a hash check works offline and cannot break when gm's checkout moves or changes; a serve-time read of gm's checkout would make fx's output depend on another repo's state.
- Comparison source for Step 3: gm's live server, read through the gm MCP tools (ReadMcpResourceTool for skill:// and run://, ListMcpResourcesTool for the list). Reason: this reads gm's live output without starting a second gm serve against a runs directory, which would write state.
- Ordering: the three in-flight agents finish and commit path-limited before the MCP build starts. Reason: their hunks share files that the MCP work would otherwise touch.

## Phase B repair: TaskOutput task_id label

Cause: TaskOutput and TaskStop carry task_id but had label_arg_kind none, so terminalSessionCompletedActionLabel (which accepted only session_id) returned null for them and the label path could not read task_id. Two tool_presentation tests still used the stale Bash interact fixture; Bash is command-only after Row 2, so terminalDisplayTargetSessionId and terminalSessionCompletedActionLabel returned null there.

Fix: LabelArgKind gains task_id, mapped in labelValueForKind to the task_id argument. TaskOutput and TaskStop in builtins/tools.zig use label_arg_kind task_id. terminalSessionCompletedActionLabel accepts session_id and task_id. terminalDisplayTargetSessionId reads task_id for task_id and none. The byte-exact contract hash is not touched: toolGatewaySchemaJson hashes model_schema only, not label kinds.

Expectation changes in tool_presentation.zig: the test formerly named "terminal session completed action label matches the interact and stop presentations" is now "terminal task completed action label matches the TaskOutput and TaskStop presentations". It observes through TaskOutput with task_id and expects the spec completed labels "Read task" and "Stopped task" (was "Observed" and "Stopped"). The Bash send case ("Sent input to") is removed because no current tool sends input; Bash has no chars field. The Bash run and read_file null cases are kept. "terminal display target is call-local across a cold inspect projection update" moves from Bash interact to TaskOutput task_id; its expectations are unchanged.

Open, outside this scope: app_session_runtime.zig tests "resume projection stores reflow metadata for session action rows" and "resume projection restores session action rows with labels seeded from the live root" still expect the action label "Observed". TaskOutput completed_action_label is "Read task" in builtins/tools.zig, so the lookup now returns "Read task" and the observed_metadata check fails. Owner decision needed: either those expectations move to "Read task", or the TaskOutput completed_action_label changes to "Observed".

## Stall record: three background gate agents (ad647133b3464d051, a6fffb445b17f1248, abd4d430c5ddf96bc)

- Cause: each agent's gate job queued on /tmp/fx-build.lock while another agent's gate held it. Each waited on a log or lock file that never appeared, for 16 to 20 minutes, until the gm job budget ran out. The agents then restarted their gates and re-queued behind each other.
- Compounding cause: stopping a gate wrapper script by PID orphans its timeout and test children, and an orphan keeps the lock fd. The first kill left a fresh fx-test (parent PID 1) holding the lock. Stop a gate by its whole process group, not by the wrapper's PID alone.
- Action: the three agents were stopped with TaskStop. Gate processes were stopped by PID (settings-gate 3733938/3733941 and 3829937/3829940/3829946; mcp-gate 3760115/3760118/3760120 and 3793740/3793743; taskout-gate 3791970/3791973/3791975 and 3795787/3795792/3795796; zig test 3811099/3811127; orphan fx-test 3831554/3831555). The lock was confirmed free with flock -n.
- Not verified: the stopped agents' edits. The tree compiles (zig build install-test exits 0 in the foreground), but no test verification was completed for them. The gate after the stop is /tmp/gate-after-stop.log.

## Admission gate repair: shell diagnostic action projection

- Failing: core.cli.cli_ask.test "shell diagnostic action projection accepts only current actions" (panic, attempt to use null value, cli_ask.zig:7966, gate /tmp/grep-tower.log line 10621).

## MCP lane: BADF fix, Zig 0.17 test-root open mode, per-method evidence

- Gate failure: mcp_server.server.test "resources/list names the served skill and the runs that have logs" panicked with BADF (/tmp/mcp-lane.log line 11042). Trace: runs.list (runs.zig:57) iterates the root Dir, and getdents on it returns EBADF.
- Cause: the test fixture opened its runs root with std.testing.tmpDir(.{}). Zig 0.17 opens a directory without iterate as O_PATH (lib/std/Io/Threaded.zig, dir open: flags.PATH = true when !options.iterate), and getdents on an O_PATH descriptor fails with EBADF. The production root is opened with iterate = true (runs.openRoot, and server.run), so production was not the source.
- Fix: the four tmpDir calls in src/mcp_server/server.zig tests feeding a Session now pass .{ .iterate = true }. No assertion changed. The fixture is a test-setup change, not a production change, because the production open mode was already correct.

## Local time: pre-1970 local dates (lane fix)
- Test "date disclosure uses the local calendar day" (src/builtins/context.zig:3211). Cause: local_time.inZone computed the date with std.time.epoch on an unsigned seconds count, and fell back to UTC whenever the local time was before 1970. Epoch 0 in EST therefore printed 1970-01-01, not the local day 1969-12-31, which row 22 (local calendar day) requires. Fix: inZone derives the civil date from signed days (civilFromDays), so a pre-1970 local time is dated in its own zone; the UTC fallback remains for an offset of a day or more and for timestamps past the calendar limit. Expectation change: "local time falls back to UTC when the zone cannot apply" now expects 1969-12-31 17:00:00.002 PDT for epoch 2 ms in PDT, since the zone applies. Witness: zig test src/core/shared/local_time.zig, 5 of 5 passed, including the new "local time dates a pre-1970 local time by its own calendar day" (EST, epoch 0 gives 1969-12-31 19:00:00.000 EST).

## Tower git: relative checkout root reached git as a second relative path

- Failing: core.tower.git.test "Tower base snapshot commits the checkout's uncommitted changes and the mission branch starts from them" (GitFailed), "Tower git worktree, commit and no-ff merge round trip" (FileNotFound at the worktree write), "Tower worktree refuses an existing branch no mission owns and attaches one a mission owns" (FileNotFound at the worktree status).
- Cause: the tests root the repository at a relative ".zig-cache/tmp/<sub>" path. git runs with cwd set to that root, so a relative worktree path and the relative GIT_INDEX_FILE (root/.git/tower-wip.index) were resolved against the root a second time. The worktree landed at root/root/wt, and read-tree could not create its index. Git identity and worktree support (git 2.53.0) are not involved, so this is not an environment cause and the harness is not changed.
- Decision: the test root is left as written; production resolves a relative root against the process cwd so every path handed to git is absolute. Same decision as the section "Tower spawn host-unavailable test: relative store root reaches an absolute-only rename" above.
- Fix: src/core/tower/git.zig absolutePath, used by worktreeAddNewBranch, worktreeAdd, worktreeRemove and the index path in snapshotBaseWip.
- Witness: zig test of src/core/tower/git.zig, the three tests above pass.

## Tower git round trip: changed files are read before the no-ff merge

- Failing after the relative-root fix above: "Tower git worktree, commit and no-ff merge round trip" asserted that base...tower/m1 lists feature.txt after mergeNoFf. After a no-ff merge the branch is an ancestor of base, so the three-dot diff is empty.
- Decision: Tower reads a mission's changed files before it merges. src/core/tower/store_git.zig observe calls diffNameOnly(diff_base, tip) on the unmerged branch (store_git.zig line 55). The assertion is unchanged; only its position moves before mergeNoFf.
- Fix: test ordering in src/core/tower/git.zig.
- Witness: zig test of src/core/tower/git.zig, "Tower git worktree, commit and no-ff merge round trip" passes.

## PNG crop: Adam7 test fixtures were written without the interlace flag

- Failing: core.image.png_crop.test "png crop unfilters interlaced Adam7 PNGs back to the source pixels" (CorruptPng).
- Cause: the test encoder encodeScanlines wrote IHDR byte 12 (the interlace method) as 0 for interlaced fixtures. The decoder therefore read a single pass, took filter bytes from the middle of the Adam7 stream, and failed on filter byte 74. The shift casts from d60dbfc3 are not the cause: unpackRow and packRow compute the same mask and shift values as before, since bit % 8 is a multiple of the bit depth and the shift stays in 0..7.
- Fix: src/core/image/png_crop.zig encodeScanlines takes an interlaced flag and sets IHDR byte 12. cropPng passes false, and the decode path is unchanged.
- Witness: zig test of src/core/image/png_crop.zig, 11 of 11 pass.

## Gate repair: ui render and transcript

- Gate repair ui render and transcript, fuzz test panics on error logs. Test: ui.transcript.transcript_window_fuzz "the transcript window keeps the model's laws on arbitrary event sequences". Cause: acp.prompt test "ACP admits default-safe web fetch without a rule" freed its permission rules only on the success path; when its assertion failed the rule set leaked, SafeAllocator logged err, and the terminal runner does not reset log_err_count between tests, so the next fuzz test panicked with error logs detected. - Gate repair ui render and transcript, 17 core.app.app_render_runtime cases fail in terminal mode. Tests: "requested-frame flush commits and acknowledges one snapshot", "first requested startup frame commits through the ordinary coordinator", "main skill menu origins share the inline footer", "settings help and resume menus share the inline footer", "roomy resume footer paints twenty VT session rows", "inline menus survive the VT size and resize matrix", "active setup hub stays on the inline transcript surface", "inline model catalog survives modal preemption and close", "file approval returns to the preserved inline skills menu", "restores file review before rendering a generic approval inline", "generic approval exits the full transcript screen before rendering inline", "question prompt exits the full transcript screen before rendering inline", "lifecycle rewrite recovers normal buffer after file rejection", "full transcript defers repaint until its page is ready", "full transcript resize defers history reset until primary restoration", "exits terminal-only full transcript state before normal render", "coordinator physically scrolls preserved shell rows for wrapped transcript growth". Cause: the test app's TerminalState used the process stdin (fd 0) for pollInput. The frame build checkpoint polls that fd, so any readable or hung-up stdin reports input pending and the frame attempt aborts (InputPending). A terminal run has stdin at /dev/null or EOF, which is readable, while the listen-mode build runner gives an open idle pipe. Fix: CoordinatorTestApp uses stdin_fd -1 (poll ignores it). Production behavior is unchanged. Decision: none. Decision: docs/PENDING_VALIDATION.md line 10 (Row 9 WebSearch, the tool is named WebSearch). Witness: the focused app_commands run passes this test.

- ACP admits default-safe web fetch without a rule (src/acp/prompt.zig). The prompt.zig change landed inside commit cab60615 with the ui lane defer, and that lane recorded no decision for it. Decision: line 641 (expectation changed: auto to ask for the asked-rule check only; the deny check stays under auto). Witness: the focused prompt test binary passes this test.
- ACP default user commands require configured authority or review (src/acp/prompt.zig). Cause: the test expected an auto-mode Bash call to be denied with review_unavailable, but auto has no reviewer and approves everything except configured deny and AskUserQuestion (Permission modes row 24, PENDING_VALIDATION.md line 641; Kimi policies/auto-mode-approve.ts). The runtime is right; the expectation is stale. Decision: line 641 (expectation changed: deny review_unavailable to once auto_mode). Witness: the focused prompt test binary passes this test.
- ACP auto mode approves prepared external file mutation without a reviewer (src/acp/prompt.zig). Cause: the test required a prepared file-mutation review packet (authorization.prepared != null) for an external write under auto. - Gate repair ui render and transcript, core.app.app_input_runtime "help menu submits an exact slash command on first Enter". Cause: submitHelpMenuSelection returned early for any exact registry match, so a typed alias such as /clear was submitted as typed, not as the /new row it names. Fix: the early return applies only when the exact match is the entry's canonical command; an alias falls through to the selected help row, so /clear submits /new.
