## MCP 2026-07-28 and subscriptions/listen stream (changes and design)

This section supersedes the Phase A bullets "Protocol versions" and "subscriptions/listen (server.zig listen)" above. The ledger is append-only, so those bullets stay as written.

Changes:
- Negotiation (src/mcp_server/wire.zig): latest_version is 2026-07-28. supported_versions is 2026-07-28, 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26. initialize answers the newest supported version when the requested one is unknown, so the test expects 2026-07-28.
- Per-request version (server.zig dispatch): a request whose params._meta names io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion outside supported_versions gets -32022 with data {requested, supported}. A request naming 2026-07-28 is modern, and every other request keeps the 2025-11-25 shapes.
- server/discover (server.zig discoverResult): returns supportedVersions, capabilities (completions, prompts, resources with subscribe, tools; listChanged false), resultType complete, cacheScope public, ttlMs 0, and the _meta serverInfo block.
- Modern results (wire.zig writeCacheable and writeComplete, applied in tools.zig, prompts.zig, resources.zig, completion.zig): every modern result carries resultType complete and the _meta serverInfo block. List and read results also carry cacheScope public and ttlMs 0.
- Removed in 2026: resources/subscribe, resources/unsubscribe and logging/setLevel answer method not found for a modern request. They stay served for 2025-11-25 and older clients.
- subscriptions/listen is a stream. It requires params._meta protocolVersion and params.notifications, and it returns only the resource URIs that exist as granted resourceSubscriptions. It sends notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged with _meta.subscriptionId set to the listen request id and the granted filter. The stream stays open until notifications/cancelled names that request id, or stdin reaches EOF. The listen request then gets its response {_meta.subscriptionId, resultType complete}.
- resources/list, resources/read and completion/complete keep their 2025-11-25 behavior for legacy clients.

Stream design (server.zig, Session and run):
- run() polls stdin with std.posix.poll. The timeout is 100 ms while any stream is open and -1 otherwise. Each wake reads up to 64 KiB, feeds it to the line buffer, and then calls Session.tick.
- Session.tick re-reads each subscribed resource with resources.read, hashes its text with std.crypto.hash.sha2.Sha256, and emits notifications/resources/updated {_meta.subscriptionId, uri} when the digest differs from the last one sent. The stored digest is replaced on each emit, so one change produces one notification.
- Session.finish runs on EOF. It writes each open stream's listen response and frees the stream. Output for one iteration is written as one buffer to stdout.
- Session.cancel handles notifications/cancelled. It writes the listen response for the matching stream and removes that stream.
- Limits, recorded and not fixed here: update detection polls every 100 ms and re-reads the whole resource text on each tick; only resourceSubscriptions is filterable, so listChanged for tools, prompts and resources is not sent; a subscribed URI that does not exist at listen time is not granted and gets no later update.

Tests (server.zig and wire.zig):
- wire: the version list starts with 2026-07-28 and keeps 2025-11-25.
- server/discover: advertises 2026-07-28 first with the capabilities it serves.
- -32022: an unsupported _meta version is refused with the supported list.
- tools/list: a 2026-07-28 request gets the modern shape with resultType complete and the read_file tool.
- subscriptions/listen: needs _meta protocolVersion and a request id (the ack-only test is replaced by this one).
- subscriptions/listen stream: the ack is written, one update follows a run log append, a second tick is silent, and cancel writes the listen response and removes the stream.
- The legacy tests are unchanged except initialize, whose unknown-version expectation is now 2026-07-28.

## Test surface: zig build test runs a minimal set by default (Phase A, local)

## Cron journal: lines fired with no open session are kept queued (Phase A, local)

- Defect: cron_drive.tick drained the journal and then persisted each line through the sink. App.persistCronLine (src/main.zig) returned success when no session was open, so a fired cron.cursor or cron.add line was removed from the cron journal and never written. A restart then replayed a journal without it.
- Change: src/core/cron/runtime.zig adds retainJournal, which puts lines back at the front of the journal, in order. src/core/agent/runtime/cron_drive.zig tick persists lines one at a time, stops at the first failure, and retains the unpersisted tail. src/main.zig persistCronLine returns error.NoOpenSession when no session is open; the replay path (replayCronJournal) keeps its silent return, unchanged.
- Test: src/core/agent/runtime/cron_drive.zig "cron tick keeps journal lines queued until a session can persist them". The Recorder sink gains reject_persist. The test expects no line persisted while rejected, then cron.add and cron.cursor persisted in order on the next tick.
- Note: the standalone zig test on cron_drive.zig cannot compile outside the module root (imports of ../../cron/runtime.zig), so the witness is the suite run, not a standalone run.
- Witness needed (Phase B): (1) the full suite binary prints "OK" for the test name above; (2) zig build test (minimal default) exits 0; (3) zig build test -Dtest-area=core exits 0 (the core area covers core.agent and core.cron, which this change touches). All run with --cache-dir set to a fresh directory.

## Phase A: tower guard, MCP subscription limits, item 4 decision

Phase A changes are committed locally and not pushed. Each change lists its witness. The witnesses are run in Phase B with a fresh --cache-dir.

1. Tower guard fails closed (src/core/tooling/tool_dispatch.zig, `towerWorkspaceOwned` and `towerLoadFailsClosed`). Only `error.TowerRefused` with the not_initialized message leaves a workspace unowned. Every other load error (lost or unreadable state, OutOfMemory, any read error) counts as owned, so the guard runs.
   - Witnesses (core area): "tower guard treats an out-of-memory load as owned so the guard still runs", "tower guard treats an unreadable state file as owned so the guard still runs", "tower guard treats a corrupt state file as owned so the guard still runs", "tower guard treats a lost state file under an existing tower root as owned so the guard still runs", "tower guard leaves an uninitialized repository unowned", "tower guard leaves a state file without a session unowned", and the existing "a write root refuses a Bash command the tower guard vetoes in an owned workspace and admits the rest".
   - Red before fix: in Phase B the catch is temporarily replaced with `return false` in the working tree, and the four owned-on-error tests are expected to fail. The fix is then restored and the run repeated.
2. Stat-only stamps and run key (src/mcp_server/runs.zig, `logStat` and `stampKey`). `stampKey` sums a Wyhash of each run's name, log size and log mtime, so it is independent of directory order.
3. Per-URI stamp and list digest (src/mcp_server/resources.zig, `Digest`, `Stamp`, `stamp`, `listKey`, `listDigest`). A skill URI has a constant stamp because its text is embedded. A run URI is stamped by its log file, since the witness is read from that log.
4. Subscription stream (src/mcp_server/server.zig):
   a. Each tick re-reads a granted URI only when its stamp changed, and re-hashes it only then.
   b. A URI that did not exist at listen time stays pending. A later tick grants it once its log exists, sends notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged for that URI, then notifications/resources/updated.
   c. When the client asked for resourcesListChanged, a tick sends notifications/resources/list_changed when the run URI set changes (a run appears or disappears, or a witness appears). The cheap stamp key gates the full digest, so an ordinary log append does not notify.
   d. toolsListChanged and promptsListChanged are echoed in the acknowledgement and never emitted, because tools and prompts are static.
   - Witnesses (mcp_server): "subscriptions/listen grants a URI that did not exist at listen time once it appears", "subscriptions/listen sends resources/list_changed when the run list changes and not when a log only grows", and the existing "subscriptions/listen opens a stream, delivers one update, and ends with a response on cancel", whose expectations are unchanged.
   - Red before fix: not run. The new tests sit beside the code they replace, so a red run would need a second copy of the file.
5. Item 4 decision: no production change. A host answers form elicitation exactly when the client advertises the mode, and never answers an elicitation the client did not declare.
   - Reasoning: the MCP spec lets a server send elicitation/create only to a client that declared the elicitation capability. The engine enforces this in src/mcp/server.zig (`elicitation.declared`), and the rejection is invalid_params before any ask callback runs.
   - Commit 6f37b3ec already ties the advertisement to the host's configured modes. A host with form questions advertises `{"elicitation":{"form":{}}}` and answers. A host without questions advertises `{}` and the engine rejects unsolicited elicitation. The advertisement and the answer path come from the same options, so the case "host with form questions, client advertises none" cannot occur at HEAD.
   - The owner question recorded above is therefore decided here, and no owner action is needed. The default `{}` is pinned by "MCP client declares no elicitation, sampling, or roots capability".
   - Witnesses (core area, runtime.zig): "an answer to a withdrawn 2025 question reaches no one, and the next question gets its own" and "a question no call can show is answered cancel, and the server goes on". Both were OK in the 6f37b3ec gate (/tmp/elicit-gate2.log, lines 3634 and 3636). Phase B reruns them. The default-capability pin is the third witness.
6. Item 5 stays open. The MCP client legacy HTTP+SSE transport and ACP session/delete need a new transport and are not touched in this pass.

## Item 5 scope (decided before any change in this pass)

- Part 1 (MCP client legacy HTTP+SSE transport): taken, implemented. The target is protocol 2026-07-28 (src/mcp/core/era.zig preferred list). Its Streamable HTTP page, "Backward Compatibility" section, says clients must handle backward compatibility, may be pointed at a server using the old transport, and on 400, 404 or 405 without a modern JSON-RPC error should GET the URL and use HTTP+SSE once an `endpoint` event arrives. The changelog marks HTTP+SSE Deprecated with a minimum twelve-month window, so it is required for compatibility but not for new servers. The explicit `transport: "sse"` config is what the parity matrix row 3 asks for, so that path is implemented. The automatic fallback on an HTTP URL is not implemented here: it changes behaviour for every HTTP server that errors and needs a live legacy server to witness, so it stays open as a recorded gap.
- Part 2 (ACP session/delete): taken, implemented as a reversible archive. Native ACP has no session/delete and answers session/remove with method_not_found. Engine Manager.delete trashes and then purges, with no restore path (src/core/session_manager/api.zig:407-412), so it cannot be the reversible design. Session.setArchived (api.zig:465) keeps the log and blobs and can be reversed by clearing the flag. Session/delete archives, and reversal is setArchived(false).

## Item 5 Phase A changes and witnesses (uncompiled; Phase B builds them)

Part 1, MCP legacy HTTP+SSE client (transport "sse"). Protocol evidence: the 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP page, "Backward Compatibility" section (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http), says clients must handle backward compatibility, may be pointed at an old-transport server, and on 400, 404 or 405 without a modern JSON-RPC error should GET the URL and use HTTP+SSE once an `endpoint` event arrives. The 2026-07-28 changelog (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog) reclassifies HTTP+SSE as Deprecated with a twelve-month minimum window.

- src/mcp/protocol/sse.zig: the parser reports the `event:` field as `Event.name`, reset at each dispatch. Witness: "an event field names the event it precedes and does not carry to the next".
- src/mcp/core/http_sse.zig (new): pure link machine (start, awaiting, ready, failed, closed; bounded pending table) and `resolve`. Endpoint resolution keeps relative endpoints on the server origin and refuses a cross-origin endpoint with `error.CrossOrigin`, so the configured Authorization and headers never follow the server to another origin. This check was added in Phase A review, after the implementation agent reported the unchecked absolute endpoint. Witnesses: "a relative endpoint resolves against the server URL and a same-origin absolute one is kept" (includes the cross-origin cases), "a request cannot be posted before the endpoint event arrives", "a message before the endpoint event fails the link and closes the stream", "an answer ends the pending request with the matching id; an unmatched id is ignored", "a stream that ends before an answer loses the pending requests by id and fails the link", "a refused POST loses only its own request", "closing the link loses what is pending, and a later start opens a new stream".
- src/mcp/mcp.zig: registers core.http_sse for test discovery. Witness: the discovered tests above run under the mcp area.
- src/mcp/io/http.zig: a new endpoint event variant; `send` delegates to `sendTo`, which can POST to the endpoint URL; the GET stream reuses readEvents, and an endpoint-named event is routed to the endpoint path instead of the message path. Witness: the sse.zig and http_sse.zig tests above, plus the existing Streamable HTTP tests in the mcp area (unchanged expectations).
- src/mcp/engine.zig: Transport gains sse with the same fields as http; link construction, dupe and reload equality handle it. Witness: the existing engine reload tests (unchanged), compiled.
- src/mcp/server.zig: Link.sse; SSE mode opens the GET stream on connect, gates detection on the endpoint, routes responses by id through the pipe handlers, POSTs to the endpoint, and fails pending requests on stream loss. Witness: compiled; behaviour covered by the http_sse.zig machine tests. Gap: no end-to-end test against a live legacy server.
- src/core/mcp_host/config.zig: sse is no longer held, and transportFor builds an sse engine transport. Witness: "stdio, HTTP, and SSE servers become engine configs; the rest are held back with the reason" (renamed from the stdio-and-HTTP test; the sse expectation changed from unsupported to an sse engine transport).
- src/core/mcp_host/runtime.zig: the unreachable SSE held-reason text is removed; `unsupported` now only reports ACP. Witness: the compiled held-reason switch.
- Not implemented, recorded gap: automatic fallback from a failing HTTP URL to the SSE transport (the spec's SHOULD). It changes behaviour for every HTTP server that errors and needs a live legacy server to witness.
- Parity: docs/kimi-parity-matrix.md row 3 becomes implemented, with this section as the reference.

Part 2, ACP session/delete (reversible archive).

- src/core/session_manager/api.zig: Manager.setArchived(gpa, id, archived) (checkId, workspaceOf, openResume, Session.setArchived, release). Witness: "setArchived by id hides a session from the default list and restoring it shows it again" (including NotFound for an unknown id). Reversal path: call Manager.setArchived(gpa, id, false), which the same test exercises.
- src/core/session/session_adapter.zig: setArchivedSaved(store, alloc, id, archived). Witness: "setArchivedSaved hides a saved session from the list and resume still opens it".
- src/acp/server.zig: session_delete method; "session/delete" parses to it; native dispatch routes session_delete and the session_remove alias to handleDeleteSession; wasm keeps its session_remove removal, and session_delete answers method_not_found on wasm because the JS host store has no archive primitive (recorded gap). Witnesses: "ACP method parser classifies request dispatch methods" (extended with session/delete and session/remove), "ACP session delete answers the native sessions error and missing sessionId with the request id".
- src/acp/sessions.zig: handleDeleteSession: missing or empty sessionId is invalid_params; no sessions store is internal_error "Sessions are not available"; NotFound is invalid_params "Unknown session"; other failures are internal_error "Failed to delete session"; a matching active session is released; success answers null. Witness: the server.zig dispatch test above.
- Stale statements to update in this ledger and the matrix: line 289 (native session/remove answers method_not_found) is superseded by this section; docs/kimi-parity-matrix.md row 24 is updated to the session/delete design.

That is a separate namespace with its own tests.

Working-tree note: during this stretch the tracked copies of src/tools/agent/ask_user_question.zig and tests/e2e/tui-decision-prompts.test.ts were restored to HEAD outside any commit (no reflog entry). The item-3 edits were re-applied to those files by path. The untracked e2e files survived. No other edit to those two files was lost or overwritten.

Item 1, issue 3 (read_tool_result query misses replay text): live repro, not a fix.
- tests/e2e/read-tool-result-query.test.ts (new). A headless `ask` in full access (FX_PERMISSION_MODE=yolo) runs a shell command that prints `Claude Code` and `--- version ---` with SGR color codes around the words, then calls read_tool_result three times: query `Claude Code`, query `version`, and a ranged read with start_byte 1 and byte_count 400. It asserts that both queries match and that the ranged read contains `Claude Code`.
- Witness (Phase B): `bun test tests/e2e/read-tool-result-query.test.ts`, after `zig build` has produced zig-out/bin/fx. If the defect is still present the first failing assertion names the query that missed. The cause is still unconfirmed, and this file does not reproduce the claude --help output byte for byte.

Item 2, issue 6 (gm skill match for a general query): BLOCKED, no code changed.
- Cause: capability search indexes only each skill's name, description and path (the Skill record in src/core/skills/skill_contract.zig:34). The gm skill's description (`Runs a long task as a gm worker...`) shares no word with `skill installation and skill discovery`. Its body says "skill" many times, but discovery does not keep the body: the header read covers up to 64 KB of frontmatter, and only the metadata is stored.
- Options, both for the user: (a) keep a bounded body prefix per skill for search only. This needs a new owned field on Skill, freed in every copy, replace and deinit path, and changes the catalog's cost and content model. (b) Change the gm skill's own description to name the skill-related terms it serves. Its SKILL.md is user-owned (/config/.fx/skills/gm/SKILL.md), so the change is outside fx's code.
- Recommendation: (b) now, because it is a content fix in the gm skill that fx needs no code for; decide (a) separately, since it changes what discovery stores.

Item 3, issue 5 (labelled synthetic answers in production, and the Bun e2e updates):
- src/tools/agent/ask_user_question.zig: `call` returns `syntheticDefaultResult` when there is no question batch and ctx.permission_mode is yolo. `syntheticDefaultOutput` answers each question with its first option, encoded with `"synthetic":true`. Argument errors keep the invalid-arguments text. Other headless modes keep the not-available sentinel, so ask mode is unchanged.
- Unit tests: "AskUserQuestion answers with each first option, labelled synthetic, when full access has no batch" and "AskUserQuestion synthetic defaults keep the argument errors". Witness (Phase B): `zig build test -Dtest-area=tools` lists both names as passing. If the tools area does not reach src/tools/agent, run `-Dtest-area=core` and look for them there.
- tests/e2e/ask-synthetic-answers.test.ts (new): a headless yolo `ask` gets the first option back with `"synthetic":true`, and a headless ask-mode run keeps the not-available sentinel. Witness (Phase B): `bun test tests/e2e/ask-synthetic-answers.test.ts`. Risk: AskUserQuestion may not be advertised in headless `ask`. If it is not, the first test fails at the tool-call step, and that will need a decision about advertisement, not a change to the test.
- tests/e2e/tui-decision-prompts.test.ts: new test "bare Enter leaves an untouched question open and a digit answers it". Witness (Phase B): `bun test tests/e2e/tui-decision-prompts.test.ts -t "bare Enter"`.
- Bun e2e audit: I checked every Enter press after a question pane in tui-decision-prompts, tui-resume, tui-host-switch, tui-slash-extra, gateway-stream-lifecycle and ui-observer. None relies on a bare Enter over an untouched default. The paths either move with Down (resolveQuestionWithSecondOption sends Down then Enter), type a digit or text first, or send "1" before Enter. No e2e test pins the not-available sentinel text. So the only e2e change needed for issue 5 is the new gating test.

Each change below is one local commit as lanmower. Its witness is the Phase B command that must pass before the change is counted; none has been run.

- Item 2, issue 6 (gm skill match), option (a). Choice: index a bounded prefix of each skill body for discovery, next to name, description and path. Reason: capability search scored only name, description and path, and the gm description shares no words with a general query, while the gm body does. The prefix is 2048 bytes, cut on a UTF-8 boundary, stored as Skill.body_index, and scored as secondary evidence in src/tools/skills/skill_search.zig. Shown descriptions are unchanged. - Q14, /plan. Commit 2b93cdd7. /plan toggles with no argument; on, off and clear are accepted; other arguments get the usage notice. Clear ends plan mode like off, because fx gives clear no other meaning. Gaps: the plan-path notice (no plan file path exists in code) and the description form. ## Stretch 2: superagent witness, use-after-move, queue head

Phase A changes (each committed locally; the witness column is what Phase B must run):

1. `src/main.zig`, `src/core/superagent/app_host.zig` (Q7): `superagent_app_host.bind` ran inside `App.init` on `&app`, a local that `init` returns by value, so the host held a pointer into a dead stack frame. Symptom: a superagent `instruct` on a live root segfaulted the process after the peer's first prompt; the skill catalog read freed memory (the second `skills.Runtime` instance was a bitwise copy of the first). Fixed by binding in `rebindAfterInit`, which runs at the App's final address. Witness: `tests/e2e/superagent-peer.test.ts` (TUI, tmux): start, instruct (`queued`), status polled until idle with the peer's `peer-pong` in the tail, stop (`stopped`). Result: `bun test tests/e2e/superagent-peer.test.ts`, 1 pass, 0 fail, wall 1.98 s.
2. `src/core/superagent/app_host.zig` (Q7): `status` never filled `output_tail` (the field was never written); it now carries the last assistant message of the peer, capped at 2000 bytes. `instruct` reported `cwd=` empty because it echoed the request; it now reports the root's cwd. Witness: item 1.
3. `src/tools/superagent/superagent.zig`: an unbound session (`fx ask`, which never binds the host) reported "could not start persistent peer root"; it now reports "superagent is not available in this session; run fx interactively to use persistent peer roots". Witness: `zig build test -Dtest-area=tools --summary all`, EXIT 0, wall 32 s before this item and 809 pass after it, including "an unbound session reports superagent as unavailable, not as a failed start".
4. `tests/e2e/tmux-helpers.ts`: `serveFakeGateway` is exported so a witness can route by request content. `tests/e2e/ci-shard-weights.json`: `superagent-peer.test.ts` added (weight 8), so the shard check covers it.

Known limitation (recorded, not fixed here): `status` reads the peer's history from the status caller's thread while the peer's worker may append to it. The read is unsynchronized; a status taken mid-append can see a stale tail. Fix belongs to the worker history lock, which the superagent host does not hold.

No native stack was obtained: gdb is absent, apport owns `core_pattern`, and Zig's segfault handler printed nothing here. Witness: the owner-flow test in item 5 runs start, instruct, status, stop with no crash, stderr empty, session alive.
2. Label (owner's "1 subagent · Dispatched"): `src/builtins/tools.zig` gave the superagent spec `.executor_kind = .subagent` and `.activity_kind = .subagent`, so the transcript and the worker counted it as a subagent. The owner's transcript names no `Agent` call; the label comes from this spec. Now `superagent` is its own kind in `tool_dispatch.ExecutorKind`, `types.ToolActivityKind`, `activity_status` ("dispatching"), `tool_group_projection` ("superagent"/"superagents"), and `app_worker_runtime` (not counted as a subagent). Witness: item 5 asserts the pane contains `superagent` and no `N subagent(s)`.
3. Project folders: `start` resolves `agent` as a folder beside the workspace (`../nygrok` for `agent: "nygrok"`), or uses an absolute or relative `cwd`. A missing folder returns "superagent project folder not found; list_projects shows the folders beside the workspace". `Root.cwd` and `agent.project_root` carry the folder. `agentWorkspace` in `src/core/app/app_agent_runtime.zig` makes the peer's tools use `project_root`. Before this, every peer's tools used `/workspace/sa`, so a peer could not read its project.
4. Dispatcher behaviour: `.fx/skills/superagent/SKILL.md` and the system prompt in `src/core/superagent/command.zig` tell the dispatcher not to read, list or search project files itself, to start the named folder, and to instruct that peer with the whole request.
5. Witness: `tests/e2e/superagent-peer.test.ts` now has two tests on a temp layout (`sa` as the workspace, `nygrok` a git-initialised sibling with `README.md` holding `NYGROK-README-MARKER`). Test 1 sends the owner's two prompts, list then start by name, instructs a `PEER-TASK`, polls status to idle with `peer-pong`, and stops. The peer's `read_file README.md` must return the marker. Test 2 lists, creates `late-project` after that listing, lists again, and starts it by name.
6. `scripts/pgso/corpus.json`: `verify-superagent-peer` added to `verification_scenarios`. The file had no classification since `872fcd34`, which breaks the rule in `tests/AGENTS.md`.

Why `nygrok` was "not in the list": not reproduced as a code path. `projects()` in `src/core/superagent/app_host.zig` reads the parent directory on every call, with no cache, and `list_projects` joins the full result with no cap. A live list here includes `/workspace/nygrok`. The owner's listing time is unknown; `nygrok` was modified at 08:01, so a list taken before that, or a reply that reused an earlier result, would omit it. Test 2 covers the second case: a folder created after an earlier listing appears in a later list and starts by name. The owner's exact transcript is not reproduced, so this stays open.

Mutation check: with `agentWorkspace` forced to the app workspace, test 1 fails on the peer's read (`Path not found: README.md`), so the witness covers the per-peer workspace. Restored and rebuilt afterwards.

Build fix during Phase B: the first core run failed to compile because `agentWorkspace` read `agent.project_root` on the test fakes' anonymous `main_agent` struct. It now checks `@hasField(AppAgent, "project_root")` first. tools, ui and minimal were rerun after this fix.

## Stretch 4: Q9, subagent lifecycle hooks in headless ask and ACP

The matrix said user SubagentStart and SubagentStop hooks did not run on the ACP and ask hosts. The witnesses below show they do, so no product code changed in this stretch. Q9's status moves to present, and the matrix rows 30 and 31 are updated.

Phase A (tests and wiring only):
1. `tests/e2e/subagent-hooks.test.ts` (new, headless `fx ask` with a saved session): `settings.json` hooks for SubagentStart and SubagentStop append to a marker file; the main agent calls `Agent`, the child answers, and the marker must read `SubagentStart` then `SubagentStop`.
2. `tests/e2e/acp.test.ts`: "ACP runs SubagentStart and SubagentStop user hooks around a subagent run", the same hooks through an ACP `session/prompt`, `stopReason` `end_turn`, stderr empty.
3. `tests/e2e/ci-shard-weights.json`: `subagent-hooks.test.ts` weight 4. `scripts/pgso/corpus.json`: `verify-subagent-hooks` in `verification_scenarios` (`requires_tmux: false`).
4. `docs/kimi-parity-matrix.md`: row 31 and Q9 present; row 30 partial (sessionTitle still empty); Q7 present with the stretch-3 witness. `docs/QUEUE_RANKED.md`: Q7, Q9 and hooks row 31 removed, ranks renumbered (578 rows).

What the witnesses established:
- A headless `ask` with a saved session runs the subagent, and both hooks fire through the lifecycle view. The earlier trace showed `observeStart` never fired in a `--no-save` run, because that run has no subagent host: `Agent` is withheld from the advertised tools there, and a call returns `host_unavailable`. That is the intended behaviour of `--no-save`, not a Q9 defect.
- The first copy of the ask witness used `--no-save` and failed; this was the test's mistake, not the code's. Its failure reading ("no hook wrote the marker") was the symptom of the missing host, not of a missing observer.
- Temporary probes (`dispatch`, `observe`, `runOne`, `runChild`, the `Agent` projection filter) were reverted with `git checkout` on the five files they touched. None of those files had uncommitted changes before the probes, and `git status` shows no src changes in this stretch.

## Stretch 6: AgentSwarm advertised though unavailable; ExitPlanMode approval (Q17 finding)

Phase A:
1. `src/builtins/tools.zig`: the AgentSwarm spec now sets `.model_visible = false`. Before, it was advertised in every full-access request (27 tools with `ask --no-save`, 28 with a session, both including AgentSwarm), but its own description says "Not available in this runtime yet" and `call` always fails. The existing unit test "AgentSwarm is registered for dispatch but withheld from advertisement" now also asserts `!model_visible`; the old assertion only checked `advertisement_order`, which the full-access path does not use.

3. Q17 (ExitPlanMode presents the plan): the gap is a real defect, not only a missing feature. `ExitPlanMode` has `requires_approval = false`, and `call` (src/tools/plan/exit_plan_mode.zig) leaves plan mode on any call while it is active. The user is never asked. The plan goes back to the model in the result. (Correction, stretch 7: this claim is wrong. `planExitOutcome` in src/core/tooling/tool_admission.zig prompts the user through `prompter.request` with the plan text, and a unit test at tool_admission.zig covers that prompt. The real gap is that the approval panel offers approve or deny only, without the fixed choices or the model's options.) The tool's own description says "Ask the user to approve the plan". Reject, Reject and Exit and Revise are missing. A fix needs a decision: the approval question (AskUserQuestion's batch request) takes 2 to 4 options, but the contract is three fixed choices plus up to three model options, which is up to 7. Left open; the matrix row and queue entry carry the decision.

## Stretch 7: superagent view, Q13, Q10, Q12, Q5, nygrok (Phase A)

Phase A is code, docs and tests only. No build, test or witness was run. Each change below lists its witness; Phase B runs them and records the result and wall time.

Changes:
1. Superagent view, status is state only. `src/core/superagent/runtime.zig` drops `Snapshot.output_tail`; `app_host.zig` `status` no longer reads the final response, and `command.zig` `renderSnapshot` prints `alive=` and `busy=` instead of output. Witness: tests/e2e/superagent-view.test.ts (every superagent request body must not contain the root's tool output marker) and tests/e2e/superagent-peer.test.ts (the status path is no longer asserted for output).
2. Superagent view, turn-end event. `app_worker_runtime.zig` calls `superagent_runtime.noteTurnFinished(agent)` on `turn_finished`; `app_host.zig` `turnFinished` finds the root by agent pointer and posts `command.renderTurnEvent` (status line plus the final response) to the main agent through `postAgentMessage(.child, .report)`. Witness: superagent-view.test.ts (the event reaches the superagent with the final response and `alive=true`) and the unit test "turn event carries the final response and the state line" in command.zig. Phase B: this is the first end-to-end run of the post path.
3. Superagent view, root-gone event. `app_host.zig` `stop` and `removeRoot` (for a root not already stopped) call `announceGone`, which posts `renderGone`. Limit: a root whose worker dies without a stop posts no event. Witness: superagent-peer.test.ts (the owner flow stops the root; the gone notice is queued and answered with GONE_ACK). Phase B: a unit or e2e assertion on the gone text is not yet present, so this is witnessed only by the flow not failing.
4. Superagent view, journal on request. `runtime.zig` `Journal`, `journal` and `freeJournal`; `app_host.zig` `journal` and `journalText` slice the root's history turns (assistant text, interrupted and compacted markers) by `offset` and `limit` bytes; `src/tools/superagent/superagent.zig` adds the `journal` action with `offset` (default 0) and `limit` (default 4000). Witness: the unit test "turn-end and journal callbacks dispatch through the bound host" in runtime.zig. Gap: the journal holds turn text, not each tool call's arguments and output; a per-call journal needs the session event log and is not built.
5. Superagent view, instruct passes only the owner's words. `app_host.zig` `prompt` checks `busyWorker` before enqueue and answers "queued behind the running turn ... do not instruct it again" when busy. The system prompt (`command.zig` `system_prompt`) and `.fx/skills/superagent/SKILL.md` say: pass only the owner's words, a busy root is waited on for its event, status is state only, journal only on request. Witness: unit test "system prompt tells the superagent to pass only the owner's words and wait for events" in command.zig.
6. Superagent view, design record. `docs/superagent.md` gains "The superagent's view of a root" (event on turn end, event on root gone, status state only, journal on request, instruct passes only the owner's words) and lists `journal` in "Use it". Witness: superagent-view.test.ts is the design's witness.
7. nygrok (open item 1). `src/core/superagent/app_host.zig` `projects` kept only `.directory` entries, so a symlinked project folder beside the workspace was never listed. It now accepts a `.sym_link` entry that opens as a directory. Witness: superagent-view.test.ts second test. A fake gateway drives a real list_projects call through the TUI with a symlinked folder present. Not reproduced from the owner's live session: the owner's exact prompt is not in this repo, so the witness uses a marked copy of the list request. The cause is the kind filter, which the witness exercises.
8. Skill-reach (item 2). The superagent-view witness starts from the owner's plain prompt with no `/skill superagent` and asserts that the owner's first request advertises the `superagent` tool. That is the peer test's gateway shape (serveFakeGateway, FX_PERMISSION_MODE yolo). Witness: superagent-view.test.ts first test, the `advertised` assertion.
9. Q13, plan mode shell read-only. `tool_dispatch.zig` `callIsPlanReadOnly(alloc, tool, args_json, workspace_root)` admits a call when the tool's `reads_only_fn` or `plan_read_only_fn` allows it; `tool_admission.zig` `planModeOutcome` now calls it with `input.workspace_root`. Before, it called `callIsReadOnly`, which never consulted `plan_read_only_fn`, so a read-only Bash command was refused in the real admission path. Writes stay refused. Witness: unit test "callIsPlanReadOnly honours the tool's plan read-only check and still refuses writes" in tool_dispatch.zig. Gap: the witness is at the function the admission path calls; there is no separate admission-level test.
10. Q10, manual-mode bypass shapes. `command_admission.zig` `manualBypassReason` returns an approval reason for `$` or backtick in any token, unquoted `*?[` globs, a sudo, doas, env, command, exec, nohup, builtin or nice wrapper in command position, `cd` into a git control path, and `git` with `-C`, `--git-dir` or `--work-tree`. `defaultForRunCommand` consults it when the mode is ask (manual) and returns approval before the read-only planner. In ask, approval means a permission prompt (tool_admission.zig:1683), so the user decides. Witness: unit tests "manual bypass shapes need approval" and "manual mode admission sends a bypass shape to approval instead of a read-only plan" in command_admission.zig. Note: `git -C` was already approval through planGit; the new check makes the decision explicit in manual mode.
11. Q12, critical removal of `.` and `*`. `command_admission.zig` `isCriticalRemovalOperand` treats `.` and `*` as critical (`./`, `./*`, `*`, `-fr` forms are reduced to them), so dontAsk denies them even with an allow rule. Witness: unit test "critical removal denies rm of the current directory and of a bare glob, not of a named path" in command_admission.zig.
12. Q5, stemmer. `lexical_relevance.zig` `stem` drops one trailing e after suffix stripping (only when more than min_stem_bytes remain), so `device` and `devices` share `devic`. Witness: the extended test in lexical_relevance.zig ("device" and "devices" share a stem; "files" gives "fil"; "the" is kept).
13. Q17, the cap is not raised in this stretch. Decision recorded: the approval shows three fixed choices plus up to three model options, six in all. The reserved labels in exit_plan_mode.zig are four (Approve, Reject, Reject and Exit, Revise); which three are fixed is still to be chosen when the panel is built. The cap in `src/tools/plan/exit_plan_mode.zig` stays 3 until the permission request carries an option list, because raising it now changes nothing the owner can see: the model's options are decoded and never reach the prompt. Witness: none needed for a decision; the panel change is open.

## Stretch 9 (Phase A, resize): settle a dirty resize when only deferred probe bytes block it

Cause (code path, candidate; thebird's witness is not in this repo, so not reproduced here):
- `Parser.canBegin()` (src/ui/terminal/cursor_probe.zig) is false while deferred probe bytes remain or a deferred input is in flight, even when the probe is idle.
- `collectResizeFacts` (src/ui/resize_runtime.zig, the dirty-resize branch) returned early on `!probe.canBegin()`. A resize blocked only by deferred bytes was never observed or settled, so `resize_dirty` stayed set and the frame kept the partial paint (title line and rule only). That matches the witness's screen and `settled false`.
- Palette close: the palette itself has no name in src; the path that leaves deferred bytes is the probe cancel without a drain (main.zig prepareApiKeyInputBoundary drains; other cancel sites were not traced).

Fix: in that branch, if `!probe.canBegin()` and the probe is not intercepting input (`interceptsInput()` false), call `settlePendingResize` (which applies with an unavailable row measurement) instead of returning. A probe that is in flight still makes the resize wait.

Witness: not run in Phase A (no build). Phase B runs the existing tui-resize witness and reports whether thebird's case passes; that case is not in this repo.

## Stretch 9 Phase A, resize root cause (src/ui/resize_runtime.zig, settlePendingResize)

Cause: `settlePendingResize` sets the resize observation to `reset_queued` before `applyResizeWithLayoutResolved`. In the settled branch, `resizeModeForSignalPass` returns null when the size is unchanged and no width reflow is pending, and the apply returns at `picked_mode orelse return` without queueing a terminal reset. The observation then stays set with phase `reset_queued`, so `lifecycleIdle` stays false, and `resizeResetQueued` never sees `terminal_reset_pending`. The frame commit never runs, which leaves the partial frame (title line only) on screen. This is the state the tui-resize witness shows (`𝒇x v0.0.16 · Run /help for commands` as the last pane).

Fix: after the apply, if the observation is still `reset_queued` and no terminal reset is pending, clear the observation and its history delta. Log `settled_without_reset_cleared`.

Witness: tests/e2e/tui-resize.test.ts "rapid four-skill resize keeps canonical skills menu content" (120x34, resize to 70x24, wait, resize to 120x34, `/skills list`). Before the fix it fails with the pre-change code (recorded in Phase B of stretch 9). Phase B runs it again.

## Stretch 9 Phase A, tmux harness: window index 0 assumed

- Cause: tests/e2e/tmux-helpers.ts targeted `${name}:0` and `${name}:0.0`. The shared default tmux server has `base-index 1` and `pane-base-index 1` (set by another session on that server), so the window and pane are `:1` and `.1`. Each `set-option -w -t <name>:0` then fails with "no such window", and the resize tests fail at setup, before any frame is read. This is a test-harness defect, not a binary defect; the probe runs of fx started normally.
- Fix: the helper targets the session name, which resolves to its active window and pane under any base index. Five call sites changed.
- Witness: tests/e2e/tui-resize.test.ts "rapid four-skill resize keeps canonical skills menu content" (run alone in Phase B).

## Stretch 9 ACP advisory caution: cause narrowed, change reverted

- The second trace (after the auto-mode change) still shows `write_file` `decision=once approval_source=file_mutation` with no `auto_review` event. The change to `fileMutationAuthorizationNeedsNoPrompt` does not reach this write, so it was reverted (a new revert commit; 40cfff42 stays in history, unpushed).
- The approving branch is `resolveFileMutationPreflightAdmission` (src/core/tooling/tool_admission.zig), arm `.allowed`, which returns `decision = .once` before any reviewer runs. So the policy classed the external write as deterministically allowed in auto mode. Whether an outside-workspace write should still be reviewed is a product decision: the runtime context says auto sends every unresolved action to the reviewer, and an `.allowed` preflight is treated as resolved. Open: decide whether `.allowed` in auto must still go through the reviewer for targets outside the workspace, then change that arm with a witness.
- The test stays failing until that decision is made.

## Stretch 9 ACP advisory caution: decision needed (blocked)

## Decision: auto mode keeps Kimi semantics (no LLM review in auto)

- Decision (owner, option a): auto mode has no LLM review. Reason: fx's parity target is MoonshotAI/kimi-code, and commit bf9f6f34 ("Permission modes: Kimi's three semantics by parity") set auto to Never Ask with no classifier. bf9f6f34 is not reverted. The three unit tests that assert auto bypasses review stay as they are.
- ACP "ACP automatic mode runs external writes without asking or review" (renamed from "automatic ask returns..."): both external writes run, no session/request_permission, classifierRequests is 0, no review_caution. Witness: `1 pass 0 fail`.
- ACP "ACP keeps the session active across repeated automatic writes" (renamed from "...after repeated advisory cautions"): under Kimi semantics there is no advisory caution in auto, so the test asserts no review_caution in any request, classifierRequests 0, 5 requests, and the target holds ACP_RECOVERY_WRITE. Witness: `1 pass 0 fail`.
- Bash gap (defect, recorded, not chased): `printf` redirect and `rm -f` on an external target run with exit 0 and no review in auto. This is the designed Kimi behaviour under the decision above, so it is recorded as a defect only in the sense that the owner may later want a different auto contract.

## ACP MCP group: encoded stall (partly traced)

- Product change: src/mcp/io/http.zig POST path. A body read failure on a response that declares a content-encoding (here gzip over identity JSON) now ends as `http_failure` instead of `broken`. `broken` was retried with backoff up to 8 times (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, 16 s, 30 s …), so a permanently undecodable body held discovery for minutes. Build exit 0.
- Traced (temporary DBG prints, removed): for `encoded` the POST ends as `http_failure` with status 200 for keys 1–4, the same retry count as the 503 case. The 503 case then finishes discovery as unavailable and the turn proceeds. The 200 case never proceeds: no tool or model event follows session/new.
- Cause of the difference: classifyDiscoverHttp (src/mcp/core/era.zig:345) returns `legacy_answer` when there is no body, for both 200 and 503, so the engine enters the legacy path. For 200 that path does not finish; the legacy follow-up after the 4th failure is not yet traced.
- Witness, current: `bun test acp.test.ts -t "redirect or answer with a bad status"` still fails with `ACP readLine timeout` (the encoded mode). Open.

## ACP MCP group: encoded stall, legacy follow-up traced (still open)

- Traced with temporary prints (removed): discovery endings for `encoded` (status 200, http_failure) run through `endAttempt` → `legacyAnswer` → `startInitialize` (`send_initialize`). The non-pipe initialize calls `startSession` → legacy machine `.start`, which opens the GET listen stream. No initialize ending is printed for any status, so the stall is in the legacy listen/initialize exchange, not in discovery.
- The 503 mode also never prints an initialize ending, and it still completes as unavailable, so the difference is in how the legacy machine settles on a listen ending. Not yet traced.
- Partial product change: src/mcp/io/http.zig maps a read failure on a response with a declared content-encoding to `http_failure` on both the POST path and the SSE path (`readEvents` now takes `encoded`). This is a permanent-failure classification; it does not yet change the witness.
- Witness: `bun test acp.test.ts -t "redirect or answer with a bad status"` → `0 pass 1 fail` (`ACP readLine timeout`), unchanged.

## KNOWN DEFECT (listed, not skipped): ACP "ACP holds HTTP MCP servers that redirect or answer with a bad status or media type", mode `encoded`

- Symptom: after session/new, the `encoded` mode produces no model request for its prompt; runPrompt's readLine times out (`ACP readLine timeout`). The test is not skipped and is still failing.
- Cause (traced): the discovery endings for `encoded` (status 200, http_failure) run through `endAttempt` → `legacyAnswer` → `startInitialize`, which sends `send_initialize`. The non-pipe initialize calls `startSession`, which starts the legacy machine and opens the GET listen stream. No initialize ending is printed for any status. The 503 mode takes the same route and completes as unavailable, so the legacy machine does not settle on the listen ending after the fourth declared-encoding failure for `encoded`, and the difference from 503 is in that settlement step.
- Partial product change kept: 540c142a (POST path) and 57248b06 (POST and SSE paths) map a body read failure on a response with a declared content-encoding to `http_failure`, which stops the broken-stream backoff retries. It does not change this test's outcome.
- Next step: in src/mcp/core/http_legacy.zig (the listen/`.start` handling) and src/mcp/server.zig (`onListenEnded`, `listenSettled`), print the legacy machine's state transitions for the `encoded` and `error_status` modes and find the event that the 503 mode gets and the encoded mode does not.
- Witness: `bun test acp.test.ts -t "redirect or answer with a bad status"` → `0 pass 1 fail`, `ACP readLine timeout`.

## ACP permission and subagent group (fixed by test contract)

- Auto never asks (Kimi semantics, bf9f6f34). Three tests expected a permission request while the session ran in auto: "permission requests reuse tool ids and session grants", "explicit rejection blocks execution with a failed terminal status", and "allow-once command approval executes with shared authority". The delegation hook for a foreground call is only `dispatched`; the `completed` expectation is removed because the product does not emit it on that path.

The read-only planner (src/tools/shell/shell.zig planReadOnly) passes no workspace root, so commits are never marked read-only.

## Stretch 1 item 1 (long-stream live-group floor), trace cause

- Trace (copied from the test's temp dir before cleanup, `trace.log`): every frame before the last has `releasable_visual_offset == target_visual_offset` and `terminal_scroll_rows=2`, so tail rows 0000 to 0046 scroll into history at rows 251 to 345 as they arrive.
- Final frame (`transcript_transition_plan source_start=345 target_start=347 releasable_visual_offset=251`): the live tool-turn floor (byte 19952, row 251) is below the committed history offset 345. `transcript_transition_hold_release target_visual_offset=347 history_visual_offset=345 semantic_rows=0` then `frame_builder_scroll terminal_scroll_rows=0`. The hold repaints the body at 345 without scrolling, so the 2 new rows are painted over the viewport instead of scrolled into history.

## Stretch 8 (Phase A): the term wasm build after ddad463f and 8c5e581f

Defect: `zig build fx-term-wasm -Dwasm-surface=term` failed at src/core/hooks/external_run.zig: line 67 `.pid = pid` (child.id is void on wasm32-wasi) and line 140 the SIG.IGN sigaction (no POSIX signal table on wasi). ddad463f's lifecycle wiring brought the hook runner into the term build; 5c8b64dc built. Phase B of 8c5e581f witnessed only the native build, which is the gap.

Fix: external_run.zig splits the run by target at comptime. On native, runWatched keeps the pid, the watchdog (TERM then KILL after 100ms), and the broken-pipe sigaction unchanged. On wasi, runUnwatched spawns the same hook through spawnHook, writes the payload, drains stdout and stderr, waits, and reports the exit code, so the hook still reports its result and fails open through the existing decide path. On wasi there is no watchdog, so a hung hook is not killed by a timer; the wasi build does not run the timed watchdog. Recorded as a known limit.

Witnesses:
- `external hook runner unwatched branch feeds the payload and reports the exit code` (external_run.zig): drives runUnwatched on native and checks the exit code and the echoed payload.
- The existing `external hook runner ...` tests (24 tests matched by the filter) pass on native.
- Phase B for every change from now on builds `zig build fx-term-wasm -Dwasm-surface=term` (exit code and output size quoted), alongside the native build and the core and ui areas (AGENTS.md, Working habits).

Other files: a term-wasm build on the final tree is the check that no other file in ddad463f or 8c5e581f has a target-specific fault. The build exits 0 after the external_run split.

## Stretch 13 handoff: palette-then-resize is not an fx defect

Status: handed to thebird. Not an fx change; no fx fix and no fail-then-pass fx witness exists for it. Commit is local only and is not pushed.

Owner of the failing rows: thebird. Its witness rows 2 (resize to 70x24 keeps the rules at 93 columns) and 3 (palette then resize keeps the rules at 70 columns) fail in thebird's browser path. The fx TUI settles in every sequence below.

Four real-TUI sequences, run in tmux (fresh session each, stopped by server PID), with `FX_TRACE=1 FX_TRACE_SCOPES=resize,frame_schedule`. Flags are read from the trace lines the binary writes; the five named flags (observation_phase, pending_settled_width_reflow, resize_reason, settled, idle) are printed only by the test helper traceSettleFlags, so the evidence is the apply and settle lines.

1. Startup 70x24, Escape past the welcome screen, `/` opens the palette, Escape closes it, resize to 80x24. Trace ends: `apply old=70x24 new=80x24 size_changed=true settled=false pending_width_reflow=false mode=resize_light`, then `apply old=80x24 new=80x24 size_changed=false settled=true pending_width_reflow=true mode=replay_viewport`, then `settled_reset_committed`, then `attempt_end ... pending_reason_count=0`.
2. As 1, but the second resize goes to 100x30: `apply old=80x24 new=100x30 size_changed=true settled=false`, then `apply old=100x30 new=100x30 size_changed=false settled=true`, then `settled_reset_committed`, `pending_reason_count=0`.
3. Busy turn (prompt held open by a fake gateway for 10 minutes), palette list opened with `/` during it, resize 70x24 to 80x24. Trace: `apply old=70x24 new=80x24 size_changed=true settled=false`, then `apply old=80x24 new=80x24 size_changed=false settled=true`, then `settled_reset_committed`, then `attempt_end ... pending_reason_count=0`. The palette list stayed on screen at 80x24.
4. Plain resize with no palette in the test harness (LiveResizeTerminal, real frame commits): after the light commit observation_phase=settle_pending; after the reset commit observation_phase=none, pending_settled_width_reflow=false, idle=true; the next paint clears the resize reason and settled=true.

Result: in none of the four does a flag stay set after the paint that follows the reset commit. The resize reason is consumed by that paint. The palette open and close paths only request a footer repaint and dismiss menus; they write none of the three flags.

Limit: the real binary does not print the five flags, and the sequences did not include a palette list open at the moment the reset commit lands on a slower terminal. Thebird's browser path may differ from these traces.

## Stretch 1 (Phase A): Q2 and Q5

Q2, read_tool_result query over color-coded output. Before the fix the live query for `Claude Code is ready` returned `(no matches ...)` for output printed as `\033[1;31mClaude\033[0m \033[32mCode\033[0m is ready`. Cause: encodeTerminalSafe writes each ESC as the four characters `\x1b` into the projected block, and the query searched that text with the SGR codes still in it, so the words are split. Fix (src/core/session/command_replay_store.zig): searchAgentQuery matches against visibleTextCopy of each block, which removes raw ESC CSI sequences and the escaped `\x1b[ ... final` form. The block returned to the model is unchanged.
- Witness, unit: `query matching reads the visible text, so color codes do not split a match` (command_replay_store.zig). Passes.
- Witness, live: tests/e2e/read-tool-result-query.test.ts, new case `a query finds text that color codes split in the replay`. Fails before the fix (`(no matches in the framed stdout/stderr text...)`), passes after. The existing `a query finds the text that the ranged read returns` case runs against live `claude --help` (claude 2.1.301) and passes before and after. Raw help bytes captured from the local binary: 22110 bytes piped, 22590 bytes through a PTY (CRLF line endings, one SGR sequence).

Q5, skill search for a body-word query. The live gm case uses the vendored skills in src/mcp_server/vendor/gm and gm-continue plus one unrelated skill. The query is built from words of the vendored gm body prefix. The first attempt used one skill only and returned no match: capability_retrieval.zig requires a body token to be absent from at least one document to count as evidence, so a one-skill catalog cannot match body words. That is the design, not a defect, and the witness installs a three-skill catalog like a real home.
- Witness, live: tests/e2e/skill-search-gm.test.ts `a query made of body words finds the gm skill`. Passes (1s).
- Matrix Q5 row updated in the queue file when stretch 1 is pushed.

## Stretch 2 (Phase A): Q14, /plan with a description

Q14 part 1, `/plan <description>` was refused. Cause: parsePlanCommand returned `.describe` and handlePlanCommand turned plan mode on, then forwarded the description with `@hasDecl(@TypeOf(app.*), "submitPlanDescription")`. App had no such declaration (the function lives in input_submit_runtime.zig as a free function over SubmitRuntime(App)), so the guard was false and the description was dropped with no notice. The live TUI showed `plan: plan mode on` and an empty prompt box.

Change: src/main.zig gains `App.submitPlanDescription`, a forwarder to InputSubmitRuntime.submitPlanDescription, placed with the other submit forwarders. No change to the parser or the router (command_router already passes the payload; its test `route passes the plan argument to the plan handler` covers that).

Witness, live: tests/e2e/plan-command.test.ts `/plan with a description turns plan mode on and sends the description as the prompt`. Before the change it times out waiting for `PLAN_DONE` (the pane shows the plan notice and an empty prompt). After the change it passes (1.7s).

Q14 part 2 is not done: the plan-path notice. session_plan.zig (read, write, clear of `<session>.md`) is still imported by nothing. Wiring it needs the verified session directory on the approval path, so an approved ExitPlanMode plan can be written and its path announced. ## Stretch B, tracing the 23 failing tui-command-permissions rows (Phase A, no witness run)

Causes found, and what was changed for each:

1. **Auto mode no longer calls the classifier** (commit bf9f6f34, "Permission modes: Kimi's three semantics by parity": "Auto no longer routes through the LLM classifier"). The trace of "fx ask automatic review receives the exact delegated command" shows `decision=once approval_source=auto_mode` and no classifier request. tool_admission.zig:1775 approves in auto mode with `auto_mode`. Every row that asserted classifier requests, classifier verdicts (caution, unavailable review, held review, malformed output, provider failure, SIGINT during the wait, review packets, review commentary), or waited for a classifier request was a stale expectation of the removed design. **Deleted** (each premise is the removed classifier): TUI keeps automatic review internal; TUI preserves completed transcript when a later auto-approved command starts; TUI isolates approved foreground commands from terminal ownership; TUI automatic caution returns advice without prompting; TUI auto mode keeps tools active after one unavailable review; TUI cancellation aborts held automatic review and returns idle; TUI review response commentary permits the exact config edit and later turns; fx ask defaults missing permission mode to auto through the classifier; fx ask automatic review receives the exact delegated command; fx ask review response recovery executes only once after malformed text; fx ask safely replans after bounded malformed classifier recovery; fx ask returns persistent malformed classifier output without execution; fx ask provider failure never executes or enters malformed recovery; fx ask SIGINT during classifier wait terminates before decision or execution; fx ask terminal automatic caution returns advice without prompting; fx ask and ACP send large automatic review packets before execution. **Rewritten**: TUI keeps amended feedback after a two-command result batch, where the premise (feedback survives the batch) still holds, so the classifier count is now 0.

2. **Permission-mode label** (commit bf9f6f34 renamed the ask label to `manual`; types.zig:2371). The settings file stores `manual`, and the Change-mode help already says `manual`. The `/permissions ask` notice (session_commands.zig:465) still said `mode set to ask`. **Product fix**: the notice now says `mode set to manual`. **Test**: the settings expectation and the notice expectation now use `manual`.

3. **Output type `error-text`** (the rows named "output type"). The product's Bash tool refuses `profile` and `tty` (`Bash arguments must be a JSON object with command and the Bash fields only.`, captured by a temporary print of the output value). The identity row looped over `{profile:"clean"}`, `{profile:"user"}`, `{tty:true}`, and the ACP row passed `profile:"clean"`. **Test**: both now pass the plain Bash call, and the identity row is renamed to match.

4. **Removed `subagent` tool** (the "trace distinguishes failed edits" row, which timed out): the product's subagent tool is `Agent` with flat fields (src/builtins/tools.zig:575), and `subagent` no longer exists. **Test**: the three fixtures now call `Agent` with prompt, description and subagent_type (`explore`).

## Host load: sample, findings and concurrency cap

Two-minute sample (10 s steps), before any change: load 5.38 -> 4.58 (1-min), 6.08 -> 5.51 (5-min), 12 cores.
- PID 2980743 (cwd /workspace/hy3d): 73.6 to 74.2 % CPU for about 60 s, state R then S, exited at t~60 s. Doing work that finished; not looping. Not mine to stop.
- PID 2981024 (cwd /workspace/extra): already gone at the first sample.
- PID 901344 (cwd /workspace/tarot): 95.4 to 95.5 % CPU for the whole sample; running about 16 hours. Not the superagent's and owner-held, so not stopped. Reported only: it is a candidate for the owner to check (a loop or a long job).
- PID 2862993 (fx, cwd /workspace/sa, the superagent): 32.7 to 33.6 % CPU, its own work; children are 2863004 (idle shell watcher), 2863005 (gm serve, idle) and the current session shell.
- PID 2982282 (node scripts/check-studio-substitutes.mjs, parent npm run check:substitutes): 110 % at first sample, parent not readable from this session, so not attributed to the superagent. Not stopped.

Finding: none of the superagent's children stayed near 100 % after their work ended, so no child-exit defect was found and no code path was changed for it.

Concurrency cap (policy for this superagent, applies to every child it starts): the total CPU of its children stays under about 8 cores (of 12). Heavy builds and witnesses run one at a time; two heavy witnesses never run at once; light work (reads, edits, git) may run alongside one heavy job.

## Loop time: tui-command-permissions measured (Part 2)

- Whole file, one run with a JUnit reporter: 35 rows, 111.9 s (not six minutes). Two rows account for 61.5 s: "interactive child approval uses the normal parent prompt" (31.5 s, fail) and "TUI trace distinguishes failed edits from failed commands" (30.0 s, fail). Both are the recorded stretch B open defects; each waits out its 30 s wait before failing. The other 33 rows take 0.8 to 5.6 s each.
- Cost of one failing row run alone: 3.8 s for a passing tmux row (`bun test tests/e2e/tui-command-permissions.test.ts -t "keeps amended feedback after a two-command"`), 0.2 s for a non-tmux row. The whole file therefore costs seconds per row, not minutes.
- Fix: run the file by row with `-t "<row name>"`, and run the two open rows only when the defect is the subject of the stretch. The wait inside those two rows is the cost, and it is kept because it is the failure witness; shortening it would hide the defect.
- Watch in the loop: a whole-file rerun repeats both 30 s waits. Run it once per stretch, not per edit.

## Item 2: why a child's approval never reaches the parent prompt (trace, Phase A)

Trace, from the source:
- A child's Bash approval is registered with `approval_registry.registerTool` (src/core/subagent/execution.zig:703-720), bound to the child's `WorkerRoute` (managed_owner.zig:708, `workerRoute(slot)`), so the decision is resolved on the child's worker.
- The parent's approval prompt is fed by the parent's own worker: src/core/app/input_approval_runtime.zig:259 calls `worker.submitPermissionResponse`, and that resolves only the worker's own pending permission (src/core/agent/worker_runtime.zig:2545-2560).
- `approval_registry.firstPendingRequest` (src/core/subagent/approval_registry.zig:110) is the only read of child pending approvals. Its callers are tests only (managed_owner.zig:1276 and :1404 are inside test blocks). No production path draws a child's pending request in the parent prompt.

Cause: the parent prompt has no source for child-registered approvals. The child's request exists and waits on the child's worker, but nothing in the parent UI reads the registry.
Fix not made this turn: the fix is to have the approval UI draw registry pending requests for the parent's children, with the decision routed through the child's `WorkerRoute`. It spans the UI approval path and the subagent registry; it is not verified yet.
Witness: `bun test tests/e2e/tui-command-permissions.test.ts -t "interactive child approval uses the normal parent prompt"` still fails at about 6.5 s with PARENT_TURN_DONE in the pane and no approval prompt.

## Item 2: the two command-permission rows, real causes and fixes (supersedes the e5cf4dde trace)

The trace recorded in e5cf4dde was wrong. The parent prompt does show a child's approval: the app lends the prompt to the child (src/core/app/app_agents_runtime.zig lendPrompt/lendApproval, input_approval_runtime.zig:257 lentApproval). A debug run of the row showed four gateway requests: the approval prompt appeared, key 3 denied it, the child answered CHILD_PERMISSION_DENIED, and the parent's Agent tool result carried `status: completed ... [summary] CHILD_PERMISSION_DENIED`.

Cause of both failures: stale rows. They were written for the old asynchronous `subagent` tool, where the child's report arrived later as a "Subagent report" user turn. The `Agent` tool runs in the foreground and returns the report in its tool result.
- "interactive child approval uses the normal parent prompt": the fake gateway waited for a "Subagent report" turn that never comes. Now it asserts the Agent tool result holds `status: completed` and `CHILD_PERMISSION_DENIED` and answers PARENT_OBSERVED_CHILD_DENIAL. Pane check is "Run helper child".
- "TUI trace distinguishes failed edits from failed commands": the child waited for the parent's later steps while the parent waited for the child (a deadlock under the foreground Agent). The flow is now sequential: child, then failed edit, then failed command; six gateway requests; the trace line is `name=Agent outcome=succeeded ... source=parent`.
- FAIL_FAST_TIMEOUT and its comment are removed; the waits use TIMEOUT again.
No product change. Witness (rows alone): child row 1 pass; trace row 1 pass, 3.6 s.

## Wait CPU (queue item: what an fx session spends CPU on while it waits)

Measured with `bun scripts/wait-cpu-probe.ts` (one line per state, debug build, fake gateway). Before:
- idle prompt 1.7 to 2.2% of a core, main thread 122 wakes/s
- model reply held 13.9 to 15.1%, foreground Bash 12.9 to 15.5%, WaitFor 14.3 to 15.1%, Agent call 15.3 to 54.4%; all of it on the main thread
Stack samples of the main thread during a foreground Bash wait: outside `poll` every sample was in frame painting (`paintFooter`, `paintBody`, `paintActivity`, `FrameSurface.validate`, `terminal_diff.flushFrame`). Cause: the activity animation repaints the whole frame every 50 ms for as long as a turn runs, and the loop wakes every 8 ms when nothing at all is in flight.
Change: `render_request.animationIntervalMs` spaces animation frames so that painting stays under one twentieth of a core (interval = 20 x the measured frame cost, floor 50 ms, ceiling 2 s) and drops to one frame a second once nobody has typed for 30 s; `nativeLoopPollTimeoutMs` waits 50 ms when no agent has work, no frame is pending and no animation shows.
After: idle 0.3 to 0.4% (20 wakes/s); model reply held 2.8%, foreground Bash 3.0%, WaitFor 2.8%, Agent call 2.8%.
Files: src/ui/render_request.zig, src/core/app/app_render_runtime.zig, src/main.zig, scripts/wait-cpu-probe.ts. Witness needed: unit rows "animation frames slow down when a frame is costly or nobody has typed for a while" and "focused UI workers retain a bounded native poll timeout"; e2e rows that watch the activity row.

## Defects found by the full e2e run of the stretch D and E tree (2026-11-11)

The full run on the stretch D binary showed that many e2e files had not been run for several stretches. Eight files were brought to the current contract (commits 0a6104b0, d446cf61): rows for the removed model reviewer were deleted with it, `shell`/`subagent`/`skill` fixtures moved to `Bash`/`Agent`/`Skill`, grep rows name `output_mode: "content"`. Notes per row: /tmp/fxconv/*.md (not in the repo).

G1. Interactive start exits when `~/.fx` is group- or other-writable or a symlink (`fx: private state permissions unsupported`), since the trust gate (34438014) became the first statement of `App.init` and used the strict settings loader. File: src/core/mcp/workspace_trust.zig (`gate` now treats a profile the strict loader refuses as "trust required, nothing persisted" and lets startup go on to the code that tightens the profile and notes it). Witness: config-persistence.test.ts rows "a profile folder other users can write is tightened, loaded, and noted once" and "configured provider interactive unsafe profile permits inspection but blocks model sends".

G2. A foreground Agent report was posted again on every resume. Cause: only a persisted "Subagent report" turn wrote the `child_report` taken mark; a report handed back as the Agent tool result wrote none, so `resumeReports` re-posted it. Files: src/core/session/session_adapter.zig (`appendChildReportTaken`), src/core/subagent/child_state.zig, src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig (the mark is written when the foreground result is handed back; a cut wait leaves the report pending). Witness: unit rows "a report handed back as a foreground Agent result is not pending after the session is reopened" and "a foreground Agent call cut before its result was handed back leaves its report pending". Not covered: the mark inside an open parent turn; a kill between handing the result back and the parent saving it.

G3. `write_file`/`edit_file` with a workspace-relative path to an external target inside an existing subdirectory failed with "approved target no longer matches the call". Cause: the re-check before execution resolved the call's path against the target's anchor directory instead of the workspace root. Files: src/core/tooling/file_mutation.zig (`prepareInWorkspace`, the re-check takes its base), src/core/tooling/file_mutation_execution.zig and src/core/tooling/tool_runtime.zig (execution passes the workspace root). Witness: unit row "prepare in the workspace accepts a relative path to an external target inside an existing subdirectory" (file_mutation filter: 77 pass); `bun run /tmp/fxconv-filetools/p7.ts` style e2e check in file-tool-paths.test.ts.

Open, needs the owner (not changed): `fx doctor` warns that `permission_mode: "yolo"` is deprecated and says to use `full-access` (src/core/cli/settings_messages.zig:48), while settings and `--permission-mode` reject `full-access` (src/core/shared/types.zig PermissionMode.parse; pinned by config_runtime.zig "parsePermissionMode accepts only exact case-insensitive labels" and cli_ask.zig:5349). Following the advice breaks startup. Which name wins is the naming decision already recorded as waiting.
Noted, by design per AGENTS.md:84: Bash runs git in the user's environment with the repository's full config; the `unsafe_git` hold applies only to commands outside that environment. `review_model` / `FX_REVIEW_MODEL` are still parsed and listed but nothing reads them.

G4. Two regressions from stretch E, found by the e2e discovery run and fixed:
- The open-work Stop handler was registered unconditionally, so `hasStop()` was true for every turn; the orchestrator then kept each final answer as a standalone step and saved the turn with an empty assistant text. Effects seen: `fx session --json` showed `"assistant":""`, and a foreground Agent result read "The subagent ended its turn without a reply." Fix: a Stop handler may carry `applies`; the orchestrator asks `stopApplies` for the turn, and the open-work handler applies only while open work is owed for that turn. Files: src/core/hooks/definitions.zig, src/core/hooks/runtime.zig, src/core/agent/runtime/orchestrator.zig, src/core/todo/open_work.zig, src/builtins/hooks/open_work.zig, src/core/cli/cli_ask.zig. Witness: tui-auth-source-selection rows "direct Responses final records replace" and the four beside it; tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle "a subagent keeps an MCP tool it selected on its next request"; open-work-turn-end.test.ts.
- The activity animation ran at one frame a second from the first turn, because the last-input time was never set for bytes that pass through the deferred or theme-monitor paths, and was zero at launch. Fix: every input byte stamps it, and `App.run` stamps the launch time. File: src/main.zig. Witness: tui-compaction-activity rows "manual: held summary", "manual cancel", "manual empty"; `bun scripts/wait-cpu-probe.ts --check`.
- The 50 ms quiet poll also slowed a resume of a long session: the history hand-off advances per loop pass, and three tui-compaction-activity rows ("auto: held summary...", and the two "a message submitted during a held compaction..." rows) timed out waiting 60 s for "resume historical flow committed". Fix: the loop keeps its 8 ms poll while a scrollback hand-off, a normal-buffer recovery or a history catch-up is pending (src/main.zig `nothingInFlight`). Witness: those three rows; one of them passes against the candidate binary.

G5. The stop after repeated invalid Bash calls was unreachable: the guard counted only the old JSON `invalid_shell_request` result, while the Bash decoder now answers in plain text ("Bash does not take argument ..."). A model that repeated one invalid call ran 12 times and the run exited 0. Files: src/core/tooling/tool_result_errors.zig (`isBashArgumentRefusal`), src/core/agent/runtime/tool_admission.zig (`observe`). Witness: gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts "shell request correction stops repeated failures after both batch results"; unit row "a Bash argument refusal is recognised by its opening words and a command's own output is not".

Observed and not changed (no row asserts them): after `--resume` a stale task id returns a bare `ExecutionNotFound`; `TaskStop` on an unknown id prefixes its error with "reason: Stopped by TaskStop"; in one `fx ask` probe a background task that finished after the model's last request produced no notice turn (the run had already ended).

## Resumable Phase B (2026-11-11)

`python3 scripts/phase_b.py` runs every group once: native build, wasm build, the seven unit areas, the boundary checks, the corpus unit test and each e2e file that is not an intentional exclusion. A pass is recorded in `.git/phase-b-passes.jsonl` with a key made from the group's inputs: the source tree for builds, unit areas and checks; the built binary, the shared e2e helpers and the test file for an e2e group. A run that is cut starts again at the first group with no recorded pass for the same inputs; a change to one test file reruns only that file. `--list` shows what is due, `--only <text>` narrows, `--keep-going` runs past a failure. One `PHASE-B <group>: pass|FAIL ...` line per group.

G6. Found by the first resumable Phase B run and fixed:
- E1 witness failed: `fx ask` did not mark a limit-ended run. The flag was set in the turn-end sound handler, which is registered only when turn-end sounds are on. It has its own handler now (`fx.ask.limit`, src/core/cli/cli_ask.zig). A 429 whose body names a usage limit was retried; the retry branch now also asks `namesOutOfCredits` (src/core/agent/runtime/orchestrator.zig). Witness: limit-blocked.test.ts 4 pass.
- E2 broke Fast mode after a restart in a project with a pinned model: the pin made the model's source `user_workspace`, and Fast is bound only when model and Fast come from the same source. A pin equal to the global model now keeps the global source; pins are tracked apart in `sources.workspace_models`, which resume and `fx ask` use (src/core/config/config_runtime.zig `noteWorkspaceModels`, src/core/app/app_lifecycle.zig `project_model_pinned`). Witness: config-persistence.test.ts 33 pass; unit row "a project model that equals the global model keeps the global source, and a different one wins as the workspace source".
- `fx --help` printed `hxxps://fx.sh/docs`: the comment sweep had rewritten the URL in src/builtins/commands.zig and the unit rows that pin it. Restored to https. Witness: cli.test.ts "top-level help aliases render the same accurate navigation page".
- Stale rows: cli "session listing pages..." now passes `--limit 100` (the CLI default is unbounded since 9df43970); the stream lifecycle correction row reads its neighbour file with `force: true`.
- Not fixed, recorded: acp.test.ts "initialize advertises native image prompt support" timed out once at 10 s (it uses the real gateway host; see the earlier latency note).

G7. thebird's probe of cda7b4aa (/workspace/thebird/docs/FX_APPROVAL_PROBE.md): after the bash tool call the page wedged (`Runtime.evaluate did not answer within 60000 ms`). Cause, read from the code: the permission wait (and the question wait) blocks on a condition variable (src/core/agent/worker_runtime.zig); the wasm terminal has one thread, where std's futex wait returns at once and `Condition.wait` loops, so fx spun inside wasm and never returned to the page or drew the panel. Before cda7b4aa the host tool needed no approval, so the wait was never reached. Fix: `WorkerRuntime.cooperative_prompt_wait`; when set, a prompt wait releases the worker lock and runs one cooperative pass per loop instead of blocking. The wasm app sets it (src/core/app/app_callbacks.zig, src/main.zig `cooperativePromptWait`: pump input, tick, flush the frame, then one `pollInput` with a timeout so the page gets control). Native builds do not set it and wait as before. Witness: unit row "a permission wait on one thread runs the cooperative pass until the answer arrives, and ends as a denial when the pass gives up"; the wasm build; thebird's `fx-approval` group against a wasm built from this commit (run from /workspace/thebird).
