## Stretch G Phase A (2026-11-11): the idle repaint spin

Found while looking at processes left by tests: an fx session at an empty prompt used about 40% of a core on its main thread for over an hour (73 loop passes a second, 5.5 ms of CPU each). This is the state behind the report of four sessions at 52%. The earlier wait-CPU work (stretch E) measured a turn whose command printed nothing, so it did not see it.
- Reproduction: any turn whose Bash command prints output, even `echo SHORT; sleep 1`. After the turn the trace shows one `attempt_begin reasons=transcript` and one `attempt_end outcome=committed ... changed_cells=0` per loop pass, forever.
- Cause (src/ui/transcript/runtime.zig): command output consolidation rewrites committed rows and `rebaseRetainedTranscript` sets `normal_buffer_recovery_pending`. The stable commit kept that flag whenever the retention identity had no publication entries, the planner cleared it only when history advanced, and each commit with the flag set called `markTranscriptDirty()`. With history already equal to the view nothing could clear it, so every commit asked for another frame.
- Fix: a stable commit outside the Ctrl-O viewer drops the flag once history has caught up with the view; and a commit that made no recovery progress (`recoveryAdvancedFrom`) no longer asks for another frame.
- Measured on a debug build, 5 s after the turn: plain 39.0 to 40.6% before, 0.2% after; with the viewer opened and closed 38.4% before, 0.4% after; short turn 38.0% before, 0.2% after.
- Witness: unit row "a stable commit that makes no recovery progress leaves no transcript frame pending" (src/ui/resize_tests.zig); `bun scripts/wait-cpu-probe.ts --check` with a state added for "idle after a command that printed output".

## Stretch H Phase A (2026-11-12): the superagent loop runs in fx's own code

H1. Before: the superagent's model received every root turn end as an event and decided the next send from skill and system-prompt text. Now `src/core/superagent/runtime.zig` decides (`reportOf`, `jobPidIn`, `decide`, `wakesOwner`, `nextStepPrompt`, `jobResultPrompt`, `waitForPid`) and `app_host.zig` carries it out (`decideTurnEnd`, `sendQueuedItem`, `beginJobWait`, `settleJobWaits`, `sendJobResult`, `handToOwner`).
- Decisions: a job left running (a live background task of the root, or a live `PID <n>` in its REPORT line) is waited on once (task notice sink; one `pidfd` poll on its own thread; 30 minute timeout) and its result is sent on the same session; a finished or report-less turn with a queued item gets that item; `REPORT: finished` with nothing queued stops the root; no report and nothing queued leaves it idle; `REPORT: open` gets the next step up to three times in a row and `REPORT: blocked` once, then the root goes to its owner. Failure, interrupt, pause, limit and question events are unchanged and keep the queue.
- Only a turn that fx sent is decided this way (`sent_turn_open`); a turn the owner typed into the root's own view posts the event as before.
- `instruct` takes `queue` (tool schema, `Arguments.queue`, `Request.queue`); a prompt for a busy root goes to the host queue, no longer to the worker queue. An `instruct` to a stopped root drops the ended instance and resumes its saved session (`ensureRunning`).
- The owner's model wakes only on stop, idle and hand-to-owner; the event lists the REPORT lines of the turn ends fx carried (`command.renderCarried`, `renderNeedsOwner`).
- Ledger: each root record gains `queue`, `sends`, `turn_ends`; a restart restores the queue. Journal `~/.fx/superagent/<hash>.journal.jsonl`: one line per send, turn end, wait and stop (`roots_ledger.appendJournal`), cut to empty past 1 MiB.
- Text: the behaviour lines left `command.system_prompt` and `.fx/skills/superagent/SKILL.md`; both now state what fx does. docs/superagent.md has the decision table.
- Witness rows written: unit rows in runtime.zig (report line, pid, decision table, owner wake, prompts, pid wait), roots_ledger.zig (journal lines, queue round trip), command.zig (owner event); e2e tests/e2e/superagent-native-loop.test.ts (four rows). `FX_E2E_BIN` points the e2e suite at another build (tests/evals/eval-helpers.ts).
- Phase A spot run on a scratch build (/tmp/fx-sa, not the validation): superagent unit filter 25 pass; superagent-native-loop, -peer, -view, -restart 11 pass 0 fail.
- Not done: status, list and journal read the roots map without the host lock (as before); a root that dies without a stop still posts no event; the wait timeout has no setting.

- The three descendants of a running command are the fx supervisor (`exe __fx_foreground_session__`, 6 MB), bash (4 MB) and the command (8 MB for `sleep`); they are gone when the command ends.
- Growth per tool step (anonymous): before 69 kB over the first 50 and 54 kB over the next 150; after 38 kB and 15 kB. Idle growth over 60 s: 0 kB before and after.

- Alive 2 s after `/quit` with a background task running: nothing, before and after. Alive 2 s after SIGKILL during a foreground Bash, with a background task, during a read-only Bash: nothing, before and after (the supervisor ends its tree when fx's pipe closes). Alive 2 s after SIGKILL during a PreToolUse hook: before `sh -c 'sleep 3004'` and `sleep 3004` (parent 1); after nothing.

Changes:

- Hook commands end with fx (5c966919, c6179001). src/core/shared/owner_guard.zig (new), src/core/hooks/external_run.zig. Linux only: the first hook starts one `/bin/sh` watcher (2 MB resident) that holds the read end of a pipe from fx; fx tells it each hook's process group, and when the pipe closes it sends the groups left SIGTERM, then SIGKILL 100 ms later. macOS and wasm are unchanged. The hook runner's nine tests were in no test list and now run (src/main.zig). Rows: 'owner guard ends a watched process group once the owner is gone', 'owner guard leaves a released process group running after the owner is gone', and the probe's `--check`.
- Temp folders (53c48349). src/core/shared/stale_temp.zig (new), src/core/images/image_attachments.zig, src/core/execution/command_runner.zig, src/core/app/app_lifecycle.zig. Image snapshot folders are now named `fx-image-snapshots-p<pid, ten digits>-<16 hex>`; the ones a process holds are removed on SIGTERM and SIGHUP as well as on a normal exit; an interactive start removes, on a background thread, snapshot folders and `$TMPDIR/fx-command-output/<pid>` folders whose owner is gone and that are more than a day old (an old-format name counts as ownerless). Rows: 'stale temp sweep removes a day-old folder whose owner is gone and keeps the rest', 'stale temp sweep reads the owner from a pid name and from a marked name', 'temporary snapshot folders name their owner and are removed when the process is cut short'.
- A session reset frees the diffs of the session it closes (afed73eb). src/core/app/app_session_runtime.zig. `Agent.diff_entries` was freed only at exit. Row: 'session reset frees the diffs of the session it closes' (red without the change: expected 0, found 2).
- Freed memory goes back to the system (d5fda356). src/core/shared/process_heap.zig (new), src/main.zig, src/core/agent/runtime/orchestrator.zig, src/core/app/app_session_runtime.zig. glibc only: the mmap threshold is pinned at 128 KiB at start, so a freed large block always leaves the heap (glibc otherwise raises the threshold to the largest block freed, up to 32 MiB, and the heap keeps every later request body); `malloc_trim` runs when a turn ends and when a session is reset. A trace of live allocations showed 0.2 MB live after `/clear` while 16 MB stayed resident, so this was held free memory, not a leak. Row: 'process heap gives a freed large block back to the system every time' (red without the pin).
- E2E helpers tear down what they started (1b298e36). tests/e2e/test-leftovers.ts (new), tests/e2e/tmux-helpers.ts, tests/e2e/shell-sessions.ts, tests/evals/eval-helpers.ts. Every tmux session, fake gateway and `createIsolatedTestHome` folder is registered; on process exit, SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP the process ends its own tmux server (own `-L` socket) or session, the pane's process group, its gateways and its folders, and removes its socket file. The first `TmuxSession.create` of a process ends servers, sessions and exit-status files whose name carries the pid of a test process that no longer runs. A session a timed-out test left is ended when its file's process ends. `Profile.close(true)` keeps its folder. Rows in tests/e2e/tmux-helpers.test.ts: 'a test process that ends without cleaning up leaves no tmux server, pane process, gateway, or test home', 'a test process ended by SIGTERM / SIGINT / SIGHUP tears down what it started', 'the next test process ends the tmux server a killed test process left running'.
- Probe (e182fc24, 6b364f1a). scripts/session-memory-probe.ts; honours `FX_E2E_BIN`; `--check` fails when a process outlives fx.

## Stretch L Phase A (2026-11-12): loop gaps, the TUI wasm path, the yolo notice

L1. A root that dies without a stop. Before: closing a root's instance with `/close` left the host holding a freed instance, and nothing told the owner. Now `reapDeadRoots` (src/core/superagent/app_host.zig) runs on each pass: a root whose instance is no longer listed, or whose worker loop has ended (`WorkerRuntime.worker_loop_ended`, set in src/core/app/app_process_runtime.zig), is marked stopped, gets a journal `stop` line with `by: root`, and the owner gets `root NAME died without a stop: <reason>`. `runtime.decideDeath` then acts: a root with a turn fx sent, a job wait or queued prompts is started again once on its saved session and its turn, a lost-job note or its next queued prompt is sent; a root with no work, or one that dies again before a turn ends, stays stopped.
- Witness rows: runtime.zig "a root that died with work is brought back once...", command.zig "a death event says why the root died...", e2e superagent-native-loop "a root whose instance is closed mid-turn posts a death event, is started again on its session, and its turn and queue follow" and "a root with no work whose instance is closed posts a death event and stays stopped".
- Not witnessed end to end: the worker-ended death (no way to end a worker loop from an e2e row); it shares the decision and the action with the closed-instance case.
L2. The job wait time is a setting: `task.root_job_wait_s` in `~/.fx/settings.json` (seconds, at least 1). Unset keeps 30 minutes (`runtime.default_job_wait_ms`, `runtime.jobWaitMs`). ## Found by the Phase B pass over the consolidated tree (2026-11-12)

- e2e-mcp-http "fixed-length sse responses complete without waiting for the connection to close" failed 4 of 7 runs on 15e4ef3c with `read ECONNRESET` in the fixture. Cause: `fx ask` leaves through `_exit` without closing its MCP HTTP client, so a fixed-length event stream whose answer was read is dropped with the rest of its body unread, and the server sees a reset. The row passed before only because each model request ended with a 10 ms watcher sleep, which 6537ed7c removed; the fixture sends the second half of the body 5 ms after the first.
- Fix: `src/mcp/io/http.zig` counts the fixed-length event streams still being read, and `readBoundedStreamsToTheirEndForExit` (called from `signalServersForExit`, src/core/mcp_host/runtime.zig) waits up to 500 ms for them before the process leaves. `Client.deinit` also reads a finishing stream to its end inside its 2 s window instead of cancelling it. Streams with no declared length are not waited on.
- Witness: tests/e2e/mcp-http.test.ts on a scratch build, 12 runs, each 32 pass 0 fail.

It passed 12 of 12 whole-file runs on the quiet host, 8 of 8 alone under 20 busy loops, and in the final run. Not reproduced on 15e4ef3c either way, because no build of it was kept.

## The intermittent e2e-mcp-verbs row (2026-11-12): what was found, and what was not

Row: "/mcp alone opens the menu, whose choices run the verbs". Both failures took 14,465 and 14,526 ms. A run with the cause forced takes 14,567 ms: 4.4 s of steps and the 10 s wait for `/web +removed, 0 tools/`. So the failing wait is the last one: the remove was confirmed, the menu went back to the list with `web` selected, and `web` stayed `connecting` for 10 s with no notice in the transcript. It is not the `Down Enter` step named in the earlier record.

Not reproduced in 250 runs after the reboot, with a build that traces every menu key (`MCP menu key=... screen=a->b`), under each of these:
- 92 runs of the row alone with 16 busy loops and two heavy e2e files beside it (load average 29).
- 36 whole-file runs, three at a time, beside tui-resume.
- 36 whole-file runs beside every other e2e file run in order, as Phase B does.
- A 25 s DNS lookup for `w.example` (a preloaded `getaddrinfo`, verified loaded into fx): the row passes, so a slow resolver is not the cause.
- `web` pointed at an address that never answers: passes.
- No new thread allowed from 3 to 70 ms after the confirmation, for 3 s: passes, so nothing after the verb thread starts needs a thread.

The exit fix (06676dcf) does not reach this row. `web` never connects, so it has no fixed-length stream; `readBoundedStreamsToTheirEndForExit` runs only from `signalServersForExit` at exit, and `Client.deinit` waits only for a slot in the `finishing` state. The menu's connect path was read end to end: `publish` (src/core/mcp_host/runtime.zig) always lists every configured server, every lock in the remove verb has a 2 s deadline and reports its failure, and the reload is applied on the next loop pass (at most 50 ms).

The cause of the two failures is not found. The container allows 4096 processes and threads (`/sys/fs/cgroup/pids.max`); the machine had been up 23 hours with other agents' work when they happened, and none has happened since the reboot (peak count since: 1213). That is a correlation, not a witness.

Found on the way, and fixed:
- A menu choice whose thread cannot start ended fx. `startVerbs` (src/core/app/app_mcp_runtime.zig) returned the spawn error up through the key handler. It now posts `fx couldn't start /mcp <verb>: ...` and returns; `startMenuTools` failing on open is traced, not fatal.
- The notice then crashed fx: `Load.start` (src/ui/transcript/full_transcript_worker.zig) freed the page source when its thread could not start, and the caller's `errdefer` freed it again (`panic: switch on corrupt value`, transcript_blocks.zig:392). `start` now leaves the source to its caller, and `loopCollectFacts` (src/main.zig) skips a prewarm that cannot start instead of ending the loop.
- Witness row: tests/e2e/mcp-verbs.test.ts "a menu choice that cannot start its thread says so, changes nothing, and fx keeps running" (`prlimit --nproc=1:` on the fx process around the confirmation; skipped where `prlimit` is absent). Before the fix: fx gone. After: 1 pass on a scratch build, 4.1 s.
- The menu row now runs with the `mcp` trace on and prints the pane status, the profile file and the last 40 trace lines when it fails, so the next failure names its step.
- Also seen: `Escape Down Enter` sent as one write is read as Alt+Down, so the Escape and the Down are both dropped. The test sends them apart; not changed.

### Risky changes reviewed before Phase B

- 5fb6e74e, a user-named skill's allowed-tools grant for the turn (src/core/skills/skill_frontmatter.zig turnGrants, used by skill_invocation.zig explicit load): Bash and wildcard tool families are excluded from the grant, and a deny rule still wins over any session or turn grant (src/core/permissions/permissions.zig decideFileTargetPolicy checks first_denied_index before session_grant_allowed). The model-loaded path (src/tools/skills/skill.zig) adds only the fork directive, not the grant. Kept, matching the allowed-tools meaning in the Claude Code docs.
- b4cf25d2, deny and ask file rules ignore letter case (permissions.zig lowerString on the deny and ask folds only): only tightens rules. Kept.
- 0e12c4c5, automatic compaction at 85 percent by default, and min(share, window - 50k) for windows of 100k or more (src/core/compactor/settings.zig reserveTriggerTokens): changes the default trigger; the old 80 percent is still accepted. Kept; the unit test row is in settings.zig.
- Duplicate skill expansion: none. skill_arguments.zig owns $ARGUMENTS and positional expansion; skill_frontmatter.zig owns frontmatter fields and the fork directive.
- Crossed commits in shared files (commands.zig, app_commands.zig, command_router.zig, skill_runtime.zig, skill_contract.zig, settings_keys.zig, main.zig): the working tree is clean at HEAD, and Phase B builds HEAD, so each commit's compile is checked by the build group on the final tree.
- FX_SKILLS and plugin bin directories on PATH: only for enabled plugins and the explicit variable; not changed by this review.


## Phase B fixes for tree 2681e870 (2026-11-12): each failing row, its cause, and its rerun

Every row below was red in the Phase B run on 2681e870 (/tmp/fx-phase-b/final2.log). A killed or timed-out run was read first (the kill and timeout markers are listed per row); none of the expectations below was changed to match a killed or timed-out run without a cause in the product or the fixture.

- unit-core, command_router: `/provider codex` now routes to provider_argument (ebf74f32 hands arguments to the provider handler, which owns its usage line); `/fork 2` routes to fork_argument (56e3d1aa); `/copy extra` routes to extension (ab5e64bd, copy_usage). The three tests now expect those routes.
- unit-core, command_specs: the catalog is 70 commands (the Phase A catalog, not 59); the appearance category has 8; `/mo` completes 4 (model, memory, secondary-model, mcp-config); `/ba` completes 5 and includes /subagent-model, the alias of /secondary-model; `/un` describes "undo the latest tracked file operation, or withdraw the last count prompts". Counts taken from a temporary debug test that printed the registry output, then removed.
- unit-core, cli_config: `permissions` (a00410fe, Claude Code's permissions block) is read from settings.json only, so it belongs in files_only_keys beside `permission`.
- unit-core, settings_schema: auto_compact_percent maximum is 85 (compactor max_percent, 0e12c4c5), not 80.
- unit-core, orchestrator (two rows, one a null-unwrap ABRT at orchestrator.zig:7040): the history fixture was 19,000 words (38,000 estimated tokens), under the 85 percent trigger of a 45,000-token window (38,250). The null was the compaction operation not starting. Fixture is now 20,000 words (40,000 tokens).
- unit-core, gateway_flow (four rows): fixtures of 150,000 bytes (37,500 tokens) sat under the 85 percent trigger; they are now 170,000 bytes (42,500 tokens). The test title "at eighty percent" is now "at the automatic trigger". The retained-context replay fixture uses `* 100 / 85`, so its window makes the 85 percent trigger equal the old 80 percent share. The oversized-parallel test keeps `* 5 / 4` because its request sizes depend on the window (changing it broke the row, as the instrumented run showed).
- unit-core rerun: the group had one failure left (the /un description); fixed; the completion filter run passes 28/28 and the group is verified in the final Phase B.
- unit-ui, resize_tests: the slash picker reads "Commands 70 · type to filter" and `/mo` reads "Commands 4". `--only unit-ui` passes 1999/1999 in 90 s.
- check-compactor-boundary: extension_commands.zig imports the compactor module and uses parseCommandPercent and command_usage through it; the script passes.
- e2e-cli, `fx ask help renders documented options through both aliases`: the expected text was the pre-Phase-A help; it is now the exact output of `fx ask --help` (56 lines). Killed or timed out: no. Rerun alone: 0 s, pass.
- e2e-cli, `fx ask explains no-save resume conflicts before a model turn`: the usage line changed in Phase A; the expectation now matches the exact stderr. Rerun alone: 1 s, pass.
- e2e-cli, `add fails precisely without HOME and on a flag it doesn't have` (killed: "killed 1 dangling process", timed out after 5000 ms, code null): the flagged case used `--transport sse`, which is a valid flag now (verbs.zig), so the row ran a real `mcp add` in the shared HOME=/tmp (the shared /tmp/.fx state) instead of the unknown-flag rejection it tests. Fixed: the flagged case uses `--nosuch` and its own temporary home. A fresh-home `mcp add --transport sse` returned in 0.24 s, and the hang was not reproduced in isolation; the row no longer exercises that path. Rerun alone: 0 s, pass.
- e2e-mcp-verbs, `help, usage mistakes, and old verbs`: `mcp remove -h` prints `[--global | --project | --scope user|project|local]`. Rerun alone: 0 s, pass.
- e2e-sessions, `a second process on an open session is refused and writes nothing`: the busy session exits 4 (SessionBusy, print_stream.session_occupied_exit_code), not 1. Harness defect also fixed: the holder process was killed only on the success path, so a failed expectation left it running (PID 713076 was an orphan from that path and was stopped by PID). ## Phase A (2026-11-13): the startup rows on the fake gateway, and the code path of the mcp add 5 s kill

Changes in this commit (Phase A, nothing run):

- tests/e2e/tui-startup.test.ts: the SKIP gate on HAS_API_KEY and its import are removed. "fx launches and shows prompt", "/help opens the command catalog" and "/quit exits cleanly" now share one tmux-only describe, "tui: startup and exit through the fake gateway", and one startupFixture helper: an isolated HOME and workspace, startFakeGateway with the model catalog, FX_GATEWAY_BASE_URL and FX_GATEWAY_CHAT_URL pointed at it, and a fake AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY. Each row asserts that the gateway served at least one request. The /help row keeps the count its run printed (70). No row needs a held credential item at this point; if Phase B shows one that cannot run on the fake gateway, it will be recorded as held there, not as passed.

The mcp add 5 s kill, code path (read only):

1. The timer that kills the row is bun's default test timeout, 5000 ms. The flagged-case test in tests/e2e/cli.test.ts (the 2681e870 body) passes no timeout argument, and the repo has no bunfig.toml. The final2 log shows "killed 1 dangling process" directly before "this test timed out after 5000ms", so bun killed the child that was still running when the test ran out of time.
2. The helper's own timer does not fire at 5 s. tests/evals/eval-helpers.ts runFx defaults timeoutMs to 15_000, and the flagged call passed no timeoutMs. A runFx timeout would set timedOut and killSent on its result; the final2 failure instead showed code null with the expect failing between tests.
3. The add flow (src/core/mcp_host/verbs.zig, add at line 836), in order: config_file.update takes mcp.lock with a 2 s deadline (io.zig acquireTimedAdvisoryLockControlled polls every 10 ms and returns LockBusy at the deadline); it reads the profile, adds the entry, and durableReplaceVerified writes it (fsync of the temp file, rename, fsync of the directory); it prints "Added"; then, for an HTTP or SSE entry without --no-login, signInAfterAdd runs. signInAfterAdd calls c.hosts.get, which in the CLI (cli_surface.zig CliMcpHosts.get) returns null when cfg.load_mcp_host is unset, and main.zig wires builtin_mcp.loadHost for some commands; if a host loads, it calls host.runtime.tools(name). That call's submit loop (runtime.zig:644) waits in 100 ms steps until the request is done. It has no deadline of its own: it is bounded by the runtime's startup timeout (mcp_contract.default_startup_timeout_ms, 30_000) and by the cancel flag, which only Ctrl-C sets.
4. Candidate delays inside the child that could pass 5 s: a busy mcp.lock (up to 2 s); an fsync stall under disk load; the sign-in probe to example.test, whose DNS failed after 1.5 s with getent here, and whose wait is bounded by 30 s, not 5 s. Unloaded, the add with a fresh HOME took 0.42 to 1.04 s and printed nothing on stderr, so the probe either did not run or failed silently. The Phase B loop sets FX_TRACE_LOG and FX_TRACE_SCOPES=mcp, because verbs.zig logs "MCP sign-in after add failed" under the mcp scope; the trace will show whether the probe ran.
5. Not established: which of these, if any, caused the final2 kill. The loop in Phase B decides it.

The code path, from the Phase A reading and this loop: the 5 s is bun's default test timeout, and the flagged child is the only thing that can outlast it; the child's time goes to the lock (up to 2 s), the durable write with its fsyncs, and the host load with the sign-in probe, whose network wait is bounded by the 30 s startup timeout rather than 5 s. ## Phase A (2026-11-13, turn 3): causes of the red rows, and the changes that follow

Causes, from the full run (/tmp/fx-phase-b/final5.log) and the isolated reruns. Each row is named with the change that fixes it. No product code changes in this stretch; the fixes are in test code only.

- e2e-gateway-stream-lifecycle, "interactive context notices stay in Ctrl+O and survive long repaint": the test resized the window and read the pane at once (gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts:2182). tmux-helpers.ts:1165 resizeWindow only sleeps 250 ms after resize-window, so under load the repaint can land after the read. The read was blank ("\n\n…"). Isolated: fails at load about 19, passes at load about 4 on the same tree. Fixed by change 1.
- e2e-tui-command-permissions, "TUI reprojects completed command summaries after widening": the test read the scrollback right after widening to 240 columns (tui-command-permissions.test.ts:1298). The reprojected row was not painted yet, so the row was undefined. Fixed by change 2.
- e2e-tui-auth-source-selection, three tests failed across runs, each by the same race:
  - "API key and fx login coexist through selection, restart, login, and logout": oauthBase was taken after the "Signed out of fx." text (tui-auth-source-selection.test.ts:3599). The logout's POST /oauth/revoke is recorded after that text, so it landed first in the acquisition slice. The diff shows that extra line and nothing else. Fixed by change 3.
  - "unavailable saved subscriptions keep login and provider selection usable" (pre-change run, c75b4c33): the scrollback was read after the pane predicate for the Codex notice, before the Grok notice (line 1932). Fixed by change 4.

It failed once in the full run (433 s), with "missing.txt does not exist." absent from the pane. The cause is not established, and the test is unchanged. Recorded here as intermittent.

Common cause: these tests read a snapshot straight after an action whose repaint is asynchronous (a resize, or a logout notice). Under load the snapshot can precede the repaint. The pre-change run (c75b4c33) also failed in the auth file, so the cause predates the plugin skill change.

Measured on this host in one session, ReleaseSafe, 60 runs each, stdout to /dev/null: dynamic fx help median 1.73 and 1.76 ms, p90 2.19 and 2.09 ms, p99 2.41 and 2.36 ms; static fx help median 0.88 and 1.05 ms, p90 1.26 and 1.16 ms, p99 1.56 and 1.37 ms; /bin/true median 1.08 ms. Lazy binding (898942b3) gave p90 2.45 to 2.80 ms against the same baseline, so it is rejected. Witnesses on the static binary, wall time: verb read_file 30 ms (rc 0); require relative 17 ms (helper-ok); package import fs-promises 19 ms (fs 19, process); multi-line import 20 ms (esm-lib-ok); host call 28 ms (aGkK); deadline inside callHost 1523 ms (rc 1, deadline message); Bash yolo 70 ms (bash-ok, exit 0); run_command with 94 explicit variables 23 ms (status 0, 28076 base64 bytes, equal to expected); fx help byte-identical to the dynamic build (123 lines); FetchURL https://example.com/ 851 ms static and 935 ms dynamic, both ok; getaddrinfo for localhost and example.com returns the same addresses from a static and a dynamic C probe (hosts: files dns). Test: zig build test 651 of 664 passed, 13 skipped, exit 0. Risks for the owner: a static glibc binary loads NSS modules from the glibc of the machine that runs it, so it must be built where it runs; the host LD_PRELOAD interposers (selkies input and v4l2) no longer load into fx itself, though fx child processes still inherit the environment. Binary size 21192128 bytes. FetchURL to localhost is refused by the verb policy in both builds, so it is not a witness.

- Row acp-run-code-source-terminator (flake fixed, src/core/runcode/runcode.zig). Symptom: the schema test passed in the CLI (fx run-code --file, 20 of 20 runs) but failed in the ACP path about 3 times in 10 alone runs, and in 2 of 8 earlier alone runs, with SyntaxError: expecting ';' at <body>:6:3. The failing request held the same body the test sends, so fx received the right text. The 6:3 position is one character past the wrapper's closing '})', where the engine would read the byte after the source. Cause: wrapBody built the source with allocPrint, which leaves no NUL byte after the source, while the shim passes the source with its length. Fix: wrapBody returns a NUL-terminated buffer (allocPrintSentinel) for both cjs and esm. Unit test: 'the wrapped body ends in a NUL byte past its length, so the engine's lexer never reads beyond it'. Witnesses: zig build rc 0, 18.4 s; zig build test -Dtest-area=runcode 37/37 passed, 12.0 s; the schema test alone 12 runs in a row: 0 fail. The rate of 0 in 12 against about 30 percent before is the evidence; the lexer read-past-end is inferred from the error position and the absence of any other cause, not observed directly.

- Row vt8-login-flow-wall-clock (load-sensitive defect). Files: src/core/auth/login_flow.zig, test VT-8(e) withheld token HTTP poll has bounded timeout cancel restart and deinit. Cause: the test bounded its waits on the host clock: the withholding server had to accept within 500 ms, the transitions had to arrive within 1000 or 500 ms, and the timeout, cancel and deinit calls had to return under 500 ms of awake time (elapsedAwakeMs). Those bounds measured host speed rather than the sign-in runtime. The one failure was in the first full core run (8015/8048), which ran while the host was swapping; its swap reading was not captured, so the cause is inferred from the bounds and not from a captured reading. Change: each wait now takes hang_budget_pulses (60000 pulses of 1 ms each), a hang detector that only fails a runtime that never reaches the state; waitForAtomic and waitForSignInTransition name the parameter max_pulses; the three elapsed-time assertions and elapsedAwakeMs are removed. The state checks stay: the timeout must end in error.Timeout, cancel must poll as cancelled on the next poll, and deinit must leave thread and flow null. Witness: zig build test -Dtest-area=core -Dtest-filter="VT-8(e)" must exit 0 with 24 busy processes running (started and stopped by PID), and must go red when the expected error is changed to error.Cancelled (mutation, then restored).

- Row native-exit-stdout (present, parity row 15 of Parity 11). Finding: no drain guard is needed on fx. The ask JSON reply goes through writeRealStdout (cli_ask.zig:4747), which uses writeStreamingAll and returns OutputWriteFailed or OutputReaderGone on error, so output is never dropped silently. _exit (main.zig:4216) runs only after that write returns, and this path has no userland-buffered stdout writer. Kimi's headless-exit.ts guard exists for Node's asynchronous stdout. Files: tests/e2e/sessions.test.ts, test "a large ask reply reaches a slow stdout reader whole before the process exits". Witness: bun test tests/e2e/sessions.test.ts -t "a large ask reply reaches a slow stdout reader whole" (a 4 MiB reply, read after the child has blocked on the pipe for 1.5 s). Mutation: writeRealStdout writes at most 65536 bytes and reports success goes red. Residual: a non-blocking stdout would fail with OutputWriteFailed rather than truncate; not reproduced.

- Row subagent-test-leaked-child (test defect). Cause: the crash test (a crash while a named subagent works records it interrupted) killed its spawned fx ask only on its success path. A failing assertion before that line left the process running after its fixture was removed: five such processes, with the cwd deleted and ppid 1. Seven other spawnAsk callers also killed inline. Fix: spawnAsk starts each child in its own process group and registers it; a file-level afterEach kills the group with SIGKILL and waits for exit, so the whole tree stops with its test. Files: tests/e2e/sessions.test.ts (afterEach imported; spawnedAsks; stopAskTree). Witness: after bun test tests/e2e/sessions.test.ts -t "a crash while a named subagent works" with expect(1).toBe(2) inserted after await childHeld (the test is red by design), the count of fx ask processes whose cwd is deleted is 0. Mutation: removing the afterEach with the same forced failure leaves a count of 1; that pid was stopped by PID. Restores compared equal. The unforced test passes with a count of 0.

- Row 292 cause, from the diagnostic run (the diagnostic Phase B run of this stretch, RC 1, WALL 29s): the first 401 emits two events, auth_required then tools (needs_auth). The refresh ran between them, so the second event arrived with the retry already used and failed the waiter with the static-credential message; the second event is the partner of the first, not a new rejection. The fixture also answered the engine's first request, server/discover, with 202, where the stdio fake answers JSON-RPC -32601 so the engine falls back to initialize. Fix: the first of the two events starts the retry and sets its partner flag (awaiting_tools or awaiting_auth), and the partner is absorbed whichever order they come in; the fixture answers unknown methods with -32601. Red check (Phase B): the awaiting_tools absorb in the tools branch is disabled. Phase A: written, not compiled; Phase B pending.

## Release CI: arm64 and x86 PGSO candidate failures of run 44946346325 (2026-11-22, tree 9368c687)

- eaadd6f1, core.tower.git Tower git worktree, commit and no-ff merge round trip FAIL (GitFailed) on arm64. Cause: mergeNoFf ran git merge --no-ff with no identity fallback, unlike commitWithIdentity and snapshotBaseWip; the PGSO unit test run has a hermetic HOME with no git identity, so the merge commit fails (git 2.53 here: Committer identity unknown, exit 128) and mergeNoFf returns GitFailed. Fix: the same fallback (-c user.name=fx -c user.email=fx@localhost) when hasConfiguredIdentity is false, and a test that blanks the repository identity before merging. Witness (part A 03:39Z): HOME empty, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1: 12191 passed; 27 skipped; 0 failed, both Tower tests OK. Red (part B 04:10Z): the pre-fix binary in the same environment: 12189 passed; 27 skipped; 1 failed, Tower git worktree, commit and no-ff merge round trip...FAIL (GitFailed), the CI line; and the fix removed from the tree: both Tower tests FAIL (GitFailed).
- 5409e4fb, core.tooling.tool_args parsed tool arguments take little more than their own size from the arena and tools.filesystem.grep_files keeps only its result in the turn's allocator FAIL (TestUnexpectedResult) on arm64. Cause: both measured ArenaAllocator.queryCapacity over std.testing.allocator, a SafeAllocator whose bucket and block sizes come from std.heap.page_size_max, which Zig sets to 64 KiB on aarch64-linux and 4 KiB on x86_64-linux; the arena's node growth, and so its capacity, follows. Witness (part C 04:34Z, the real parseToolArgsObject, 200 calls): page_size_max=4096 arena_capacity=68200, page_size_max=65536 arena_capacity=122520 against the bound 102400, so the old test fails exactly with the aarch64 page size; a FixedBufferAllocator used 49596 bytes under both. Fix: both tests bound the bytes taken from a FixedBufferAllocator (the buffer size is the bound for tool_args, end_index growth under 64 KiB per call for grep_files). Red (part B): tool_args buffer cut to 20*512 FAIL (OutOfMemory); grep_files bound cut to 64 FAIL (TestUnexpectedResult).
- c78ad9cc and 9368c687, Linux x86_64 PGSO candidate: The hosted runner lost communication with the server, twice, 71m33s and 71m36s into step 7, and the server received no step 7 line. In both runs the log ends inside the 16000 line fixture of step 5 (2616/16000 and 2610/16000), which test_the_first_run_log_keeps_every_test_of_a_long_run writes twice, about 32000 lines in seconds; arm64 received all of it. Ruled out here: a hang of the plain ReleaseSafe suite with stdin held open as the driver runs it (part C: 12191 passed; 0 failed in 252 s) and an environment dependence of the suite (part A, identity-less environment, 0 failed). Changes: the fixture's stream goes to a captured buffer (lines that test writes to the runner log: 32012 before, 5 after), and a timed out command now prints the last 40 lines it wrote before it is killed, so a hang names its test in the step log. Not proven: that the burst is what stalled the x86 runner; the first hosted x86 run after this push is the witness.

## edgejs swap, stage 0, fx spike (2026-11-22, Phase A, not built yet)

- Plan: /workspace/hyperagent/specs/edgejs-swap.md stage 0, fx part. txiki stays in place and the default build is unchanged: the edgejs route exists only with -Dedgejs=<dir>.
- Source: gm's pinned edgejs (57af3635, napi f33cd8af, quickjs fcf16049) under /workspace/tmp/gm/edgejs; gm's quickjs build is queued in its own tickets, so fx links nothing yet.
- Embedding: edgejs has no public embedding API beyond node_api.h; its CLI path RunWithFreshEnv is private to edge_cli.cc but every call it makes is in public headers. native/edgejs/fx_edge.cc repeats that sequence (EdgeInitializeCliProcess, OpenSSL init, unofficial_napi_configure_runtime, unofficial_napi_create_env, EdgeAttachEnvironmentForRuntime), installs globalThis.fxHost.call(name, argsJson) with napi_create_function, runs an fx prelude, then EdgeRunScriptFileWithLoop. The shim is compiled with g++ from the edge_cli target's flags because the edgejs libraries are gcc builds and the calls pass std::string, which zig c++ (libc++) cannot share. src/core/runcode/edge.zig exports fx_edge_host_call, which calls the same Verbs.invoke run_code uses, so every verb passes host_verb_gate and tool admission. fx run-code --engine edge --file <path> selects it; build.zig -Dedgejs links fx_edge.o and every static library in the directory, dynamically against system libstdc++.
- Permission-gate options and their checks (scripts/edgejs-witness.sh): a fx verb through fxHost.call (fs_write refused in ask, admitted in yolo); a host-module refusal list in the prelude through module.registerHooks (node:child_process refused in ask, loads in yolo); routing permission-bearing Node APIs through fx verbs only (node:fs refused in ask, writes in yolo). Safe mode under Wasmer cannot be tested with this native quickjs build (EDGE_QUICKJS_WEBASSEMBLY off).
- Size: the default fx is 20,429,200 bytes (st12 prefix, tree 1a3dd801); the edgejs build's size is recorded by the witness.
- Witness and red: pending the gated window after gm's edgejs build lands. Verified so far: zig fmt and zig ast-check on edge.zig, run_code.zig and build.zig, sh -n on the witness, and the edge prelude unit test written beside edge.zig (runs only in -Dedgejs builds).

## fx run_code only, stages 1 to 3 (specs/fx-run-code-only.md), held as a patch

- State: /workspace/tmp/fx/run-code-only-stages-1-3.patch (56 files, +1648/-215) applies with git apply --check on HEAD. It is kept out of the tree so the queued window st13 (ticket 1271857) builds only the commits it was filed for. It is committed once st13 leaves the queue, and it joins the next window.
- Stage 1: every model request carries exactly run_code. vision and MCP tools are verbs, always-loaded MCP schemas are no longer sent, and the subagent opt-outs and run_code_surface are removed. A verb outside a child's or profile's allowlist returns EFX_TOOL_NOT_ADMITTED. verbs({names:true}) gives names and verbs({name}) a description and schema. The run_code description is generated. With pending images on the run_code surface, the vision mode becomes optional with a gm.vision hint, so the model is no longer forced to look first.
- Stage 2: each inner verb goes through the interactive permission path, which names the verb. PreToolUse and PostToolUse fire under the inner name, and inner ids are {parent}:{n}. Unknown arguments are refused by name for run_code, host verbs, write_file and edit_file. Load errors name the file and line. A batching notice appears from the third single-verb body. The paging notice names gm.read_tool_result. Background-after-timeout is not ported: fx has no 120 s MCP call limit.
- Stage 3: one presenter (src/core/tooling/run_code_presentation.zig) serves the TUI and ACP. A call ledger of up to 50 inner calls rides the result JSON. In ACP the kind is execute and inner-call lines go in the completion content, because ACP has no nested calls.

## Duplicate body decision and gateway replay question (tree f6539294)

- Duplicate body (decided by me, per the owner's instruction): the ledger's blob is the single stored copy of a verb body past max_inline_output_bytes (8 KiB). The outer run_code value carries the existing stored-result pointer (formatStoredResultOutput: preview, handle, stored bytes) instead of a verbatim second copy. Why this follows the rule: commit 0e962248 states "no whole file copy is made past the cap". The change is in src/tools/runcode/call_ledger.zig (recordSubstitution, substituteStoredBodies). It replaces only a verbatim JSON-escaped copy of the stored body in the report, so a script that transforms the body keeps its own new value. Commit f6539294. Unit test: "a stored verb body the script returns is replaced by its pointer in the report". Witness: the f36-gateway-stream-lifecycle and st38 runs (pending).
- Gateway replay (owner question): tests gateway-stream-lifecycle 6719 and 6726 expect RETAINED_COMPACTION_SIGNATURE (the reasoning replay of the step whose tool result is still pending) to reach the request after compaction. The product drops provider replay when some tool calls of a step have no result (src/core/agent/runtime/execution_memory.zig:637-657, reason interrupted_incomplete_association), because a provider rejects a tool call without its result. Recommendation: keep the product rule and change the test to expect the replay after the tool result is in. Not changed: this weakens an assertion, so it needs the owner's approval.

## f36 tui-command-permissions: both causes and fixes (ticket 17473, st36)

- Failure 1, "TUI keeps command output exclusive to Ctrl-O through resize and resume" (line 1176): cause. The failed command row read "Exited 7 command" with no script name, because the run_code call had no target and the failed command's name was not used. Fix: 81c2dd8e (src/core/agent/runtime/tool_presentation.zig, commandTextFromResult used as the target of a failed command row when the call has none; unit test "a command result's command text names a failed command row"). Closed by the same commit series as failure 2 (34b8907d records it).
- Failure 2, "fx ask yolo executes pwd through the default user profile with process-scoped replay" (line 2555): tool_calls[0].command_result was undefined on a successful run. Cause: run_code.zig kept an inner command result only for a failed call (ae0ece08), and counted a kept result as the failure signal, so a successful command reported no command_result while the direct command path does. Fix: 055ff130 (run_code tracks command_failed; keeps the inner result either way; a failed result wins over a later success; succeeds when the body succeeded and no inner command failed; unit test "a successful inner command's result json reaches the run_code result without failing it"). No test weakened.
- Checked: every other reader of command_result_json checks status first or is on the error path (tool_runtime classifyReturnedToolCallOutcome, cli_ask.zig:3272, 3385), so the success result does not turn into a failure elsewhere.
- Witness: pending. Window fx-st40 on the head at its start (includes 81c2dd8e and 055ff130), then f40-tui-command-permissions.

## Background unit test: cause and fix (round 6, after fx-st42)

- fx-st42 numbers (ticket 156858, head df20e55b): build exit 0 (831 s); suite 12269 passed, 27 skipped, 1 failed; txiki witness passed. The one failure is wait_for "a completion WaitFor returns is not queued again as a notice" in its finished-task form.
- Cause (corrected): a WaitFor call with a task id returns the task's output (shell.readTaskOutput), not the completion event. Only the any-event wait (no task id) returns the notice JSON. The finished-task form therefore asserted an event the call cannot return. bdccae4e changed the test to a running task, but still passed a task id, so it had the same fault. My earlier note that bdccae4e fixed this was wrong.
- Fix: the call is now runWaitFor with {"timeout":5}, no task id. Assertions unchanged: the returned body contains "event":"completed", and no queued notice carries it. Commit: see the next commit. Witness: pending a unit run on a window built after this commit (held by the swap hold).

## tui-resume: G1 fix (diff handoff carry), commit b98da0e4 (round 6)

- Cause (G1, confirmed): runInnerCall (src/core/tooling/tool_runtime.zig) returned the inner write's diff counts and command presentation but not its committed_file_handoff, so the outer run_code result had no handoff to save the full diff from.
- Fix (b98da0e4): the inner reply carries the handoff; the run_code bridge keeps a deep copy (parallel_execution.duplicateCommittedFileHandoff, now pub) when exactly one inner write produced one; the run_code dispatch reports it through a new committed_file_handoff_sink; toolExecutionResultFromDispatch carries it into the outer ToolExecutionResult. A run with more than one inner write keeps no handoff (owner question: which handoff wins for multi-file runs).
- Witness: fx-st43 queued on b98da0e4 (window build and unit suite), then f43-tui-resume on the st43 binary. The per-file witness is pending. No unit test was added for the carry; the e2e rows (large-file edit, file terminal sequences, recorded diffs, large snapshots) are the witness.
- Groups G2 to G8 remain as recorded in commit 078beae7.
